items.statement: Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid projects commissioning expected in Q2 FY27, no further delays anticipated.
items.quote: Commissioning is expected in Q2 FY '27, and both projects remain within the approved capex envelope.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 800-1,000 crore including maintenance; normal capex thereafter.
items.quote: So there is almost INR 800 crores to INR1,000 crores capex spending, including maintenance.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN capacity utilization to reach 90-95% by end of FY27.
items.quote: We expect by end of this year, we should be at least touching 90% to 95% utilization on a TPD basis.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from Equinor gas contract and global supply tightness.
items.quote: But if you're looking holistically, the margin improvement is certain and that will get reflected in our consolidated chemical portfolio.

items.statement: TAN demand to continue, though Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; no long-term demand destruction.
items.quote: This trend is likely to continue. Although we are getting into a soft season, as you know, we are getting into monsoon. So Q2 is cyclically and seasonally weaker in terms of demand, but we don't see any long-term demand destruction for any reason.

items.statement: IPA prices to remain elevated for some time due to RGP shortage; new normal expected post normalization.
items.quote: So will the price will remain elevated for some time? Yes, price will remain elevated for some time before the situation becomes normal and then we'll have to see what will be the normal IPA prices once things go back.

items.statement: Specialty and Croptek share of Crop Nutrition revenue increased to 33% from 30%.
items.quote: Specialty and Croptek now contributes around 33% of segment revenue, up from 30% previous year, which is a very important structural level lever for improving margins over time.

items.statement: B2C segment share of Mining Chemicals revenue increased to 16% from 13%.
items.quote: The B2C segment continued to scale well, now contributes around 16% of the revenue compared to 13% last year.

items.statement: Project timeline realigned due to skilled labor shortage from elections; now back to full execution.
items.quote: Now while the project execution is going strong, we do have a little time realignment due to severe shortage of skilled contract manpower, which we face with various states going in for elections and suddenly, there was a severe shortage with West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and other elections and also some impact that emerged

items.statement: Demerger or subsidiary listing not immediate; form and timing yet to be decided.
items.quote: No, not immediately. In fact, we yet to take a call in terms of form and shape and timing of subsidiary listing and demerger or listing, I call it, not demerger, how and when it has to happen.

items.statement: Ammonia business margins significantly better than previously discussed due to current upcycle.
items.quote: But yes, our margin in ammonia business will be significantly better than what we used to discuss or what we used to talk about.

items.statement: Chardham Chemicals acquisition valued for land, licenses, plant, location, and speed to market; no revenue last year.
items.quote: But what it is made up of is it's the value of the land. It is the value of the licenses. It is the value of some plants and equipment. It is the value of the location of the facility, which is the proximity to the market.

items.statement: CCDs of INR800 crores issued to third party and promoter; conversion after ~30 months.
items.quote: The split was INR 500 crores was issued and subscribed by third party and INR300 crores by promoter entity.

items.statement: Expects INR850-900 crores inflow from Dubai project over next six months, entirely for deleveraging.
items.quote: And we expect that about INR850 crores to INR900 crores should flow into us over the next six months.

items.statement: After Dubai and associate inflows, external borrowings expected at INR700-800 crores by year-end.
items.quote: So we expect that our external borrowings will be in the range of around INR700 crores and INR800 crores which we are able to manage from our operations.

items.statement: Estimated profit from Dubai project post completion around INR600 crores; capital invested INR270-275 crores.
items.quote: So, since we are a 50% JV partner, our share of the profit, the estimated profit post completion should be around about INR600 odd crores.

items.statement: Real estate development management EBITDA margins typically 70-75%.
items.quote: Typically our -- being a service revenue, typically our EBITDA margins are in the range of about 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Hyderabad and Kolkata real estate projects to complete in about five years; Bangalore plotted development in 18 months.
items.quote: the Hyderabad, Kolkata ones will take about five years f or completion, and this revenue of the top line will be recognized over a period of 5 years, based on the sales velocity.

items.statement: No major ethanol expansion plans; capitalizing existing plant with syrup and B-heavy diversion.
items.quote: Right now, we are not having any major expansion plans. Since Zuari has already having a joint venture in Envien.

items.statement: Ethanol sector has ~100% overcapacity; OMC tenders not coming; expects improvement with higher blending.
items.quote: And we understand that now that capacity stands increased to about 2,000 crores liters. So it's almost like a 100% over capacity currently in ethanol.

items.statement: Sugar prices expected stable near-term; closing stocks ~5.6 million tons, about two months consumption.
items.quote: Sugar prices are expected to remain stable in the near-term as closing stocks are estimated at about 5.6 million ton, which was 5.3 million ton last year, which is equivalent to about two months of consumption.

items.statement: Stagnant ethanol prices pressure profitability; expects long-overdue revision in ethanol prices.
items.quote: While stagnant ethanol prices have continued to put some pressure on profitability, we remain quite optimistic as I said earlier about the sector outlook.

items.statement: Macroeconomic situation affecting capex plans in India and Middle East; increased input prices for sugar business.
items.quote: Looking ahead, I think the macroeconomic situation, of course, is a concern to all of us. It is affecting capex plans both in India and the Middle East.

items.statement: Goa land bank 260 acres, book value INR163 crores; no monetization factored in future plans.
items.quote: So currently Zuari Industries is holding around 260 acres of land parcel and the value in the books of account is around INR163 crores.

items.statement: Sugar division achieved highest ever capacity utilization of 101.7% and record crushing.
items.quote: The best part was that we achieved the highest ever capacity utilization of 101.7%.

items.statement: Ethanol distillery ran 316 days, highest ever, with production of 372 lakh liters.
items.quote: 316 days, which probably was the highest ever performance.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% top-line growth, revenue INR750-800 crores, and 20%+ EBITDA margins for FY27.
items.quote: We have set a growth target of 20% to 25% on top line over last year, which would result in a revenue of around INR750 crores to INR800 crores. We hope to continue EBITDA margins of 20% plus.

items.statement: Targets order intake of INR800-1,000 crores for FY27, with INR450-500 crores expected by Q2.
items.quote: And as I mentioned, we are targeting an order intake of around INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex of ~INR40 crores for FY27; Saravali and M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansions to complete by Q2.
items.quote: It remains the same what we've been guiding for in the last 2, 3 calls, which is around 40 crores odd.

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA margins of 22-23%, including other income, with 20%+ as buffer.
items.quote: We have also mentioned we are looking at maintaining margins of 22%, 23% in all our commentary.

items.statement: Strong inquiry pipeline of INR4,000+ crores across sectors like fertilizer, nuclear, petrochemicals.
items.quote: We continue to have a strong inquiry pipeline of INR4,000 crores plus at a consol level across various sectors.

items.statement: Exports expected to contribute 30-40% of revenue in future.
items.quote: We believe exports will play a critical role going into the future. And we think 30% to 40% of our revenue can come from exports.

items.statement: No cost pass-through; mitigates risk by booking materials immediately upon order receipt.
items.quote: Our costs are not passed through, okay? We mitigate all the risk by placing orders on time.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield faced dispatch delays due to Middle East logistics, expected to normalize by H1 FY27.
items.quote: That impacted our revenue a bit in Q4 for the subsidiary, which hopefully will also get mitigated by second quarter of this year.

items.statement: No further dilution expected; all warrant conversions completed and funds being utilized for growth.
items.quote: All warrant conversions have happened. So there's no further dilution expected.

items.statement: Working capital days to reduce as large receivables, including INR50-60 crores from Moroccan order, are collected.
items.quote: The end of the year included some large orders like the Moroccan order, which nearly INR50 crores to INR60 crores is receivable in the next 2 to 3 months.

items.statement: Nuclear orders execution to take over a year; 2-3 projects in pipeline.
items.quote: I expect then that it would take another year plus for the complete execution.

items.statement: M.E. Energy expects more orders from ferrous alloy and steel sectors in first 8-9 months of FY27.
items.quote: For the early part of this financial year, maybe first 8, 9 months, we'll have more larger value orders from ferrous alloys industries or steel industry rather than cement industry

items.statement: Granules India order remains on hold with no change in status.
items.quote: It is still at the same level, status quo.

items.statement: Expects 16% EBITDA margin for entire business excluding Omeras within 2 years.
items.quote: Yes, that would be correct. That would be correct. Again, 16% EBITDA margins, I would expect from the entire business with the exception of Omeras because Omeras is right now in the turnaround mode.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to exceed INR2,000 crores in 2 years including Omeras.
items.quote: I think if we do less than INR2,000 crores, we will be disappointed. I think -- but this would -- but I would only -- the only difference would be I would include Omeras in the INR2,000 crores number.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 14-15% next year.
items.quote: Will be in the range of between 14% and 15% on a consol basis.

items.statement: Heat transfer business to grow 15-20% for next 2 years.
items.quote: So, I think we expect the heat transfer business overall to grow at a 15% to 20% range for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR681.6 crores as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: Our consolidated order book stood at approximately INR681.6 crores as of March 31, 2026, providing healthy visibility for FY27 and reinforcing confidence in our future growth trajectory.

items.statement: Omeras order book around INR78 crores, doubled from Dec 2025 to Mar 2026.
items.quote: Also, the current order book at Omeras is around INR78 crores, which provides an encouraging visibility for FY27 and creates a stable base for profitable plant operations in the coming months.

items.statement: Omeras expected to achieve double-digit margins next financial year.
items.quote: In terms of getting to double-digit margins, I would expect that to happen in the next financial year for Omeras on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: Omeras EBITDA breakeven at annual revenue of INR200-225 crores.
items.quote: So, that's our rough breakeven calculation. Of course, it depends on margins and some dynamics of the business. But probably that's the kind of number that we are looking at, which effectively means that at roughly about INR200 crores, INR225 crores kind of an annual revenue, Omeras will be at EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: Gas price increases largely passed on to customers.
items.quote: Yes. So, the gas prices have definitely increased. We, as with so many other things that have changed because of the recent conflict in Iran. Now so far, we have been able to pass on the price increases to a large extent, but so there has been the impact.

items.statement: Pharma API sector driving growth; specialty chemicals gradual recovery; agrochemicals subdued.
items.quote: So, most of the capex currently in India is happening in the pharma sector, API, I should say. There is also demand in the custom manufacturing sector. I think as I explained, the specialty and the agro are in some form not keeping up with the pace of the others.

items.statement: Thaletec products contributed ~20% of India glass lined products this year.
items.quote: And this year, Thaletec products have contributed close to about 20% of the overall Glass Lined India products.

items.statement: India capex for Omeras tanks to be commercially operational by end of FY27.
items.quote: Yes. We expect to be commercially operational by the end of this financial year. So, this will -- the capex in India will probably reflect in next year's financials from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causing some companies to defer decisions, especially CDMO and agrochemical.
items.quote: I mean everything was going well until about February. What we are seeing is some companies are deferring some decisions because of the ongoing geopolitical situation. So, while the -- I mean pharma -- the pharmaceutical and the API sectors are not yet doing that, but especially the CDMO or the agrochemical companies,

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 55% for FY26.
items.quote: Further, the Board has recommended a dividend of 55% for FY26, reflecting our confidence in the long-term fundamentals and cash flow generation capabilities of the business.

items.statement: Expects double-digit year-on-year revenue growth, though not as high as Q4's 35% jump.
items.quote: But yes, on year-on-year growth, we will have a double-digit growth as we have explained in our previous call as well.

items.statement: Expects 25-30% ADR growth from organic and refurbishment benefits.
items.quote: So, in combination of all three, as and when the new inventory comes in, I think we can expect anywhere between 25% to 30% growth in ADR.

items.statement: Plans to invest over INR 100 crores in phased renovations across properties.
items.quote: We outlined a plan to invest 100 plus crores to renovate and upgrade existing properties in three phases.

items.statement: Second phase of renovation at Marriott Hyderabad to complete in FY27; third phase in FY28.
items.quote: Building on this progress, the second phase of renovation at Marriott Hyderabad commenced in the first week of April and is expected to be completed during FY '27, while the third phase is targeted for completion during FY '28.

items.statement: Convention center renovation to finish by end of FY27, with investment recouped in 1.5 years.
items.quote: We look to finish this renovation by the end of this year. And we look to recoup the investment made into this in a period of one and a half year.

items.statement: Expects twofold increase in EBITDA from new convention center and Marriott renovation.
items.quote: We are going to see a substantial twofold increase in the EBITDAs because of this addition.

items.statement: F&B margin is 45-50%, with gross margin close to 85%.
items.quote: The margin in F&B is about 45% to 50%. And the gross margin is close to 85%.

items.statement: Expects demand to recover in next couple of months and ADR to return to earlier levels by year-end.
items.quote: But ideally, we'd like to believe that for the next couple of months, we will see some of the demand start coming back. And once the wedding season and a lot of other domestic corporate events start coming back towards the end of the year, I feel that the ADR will go back to the earlier numbers.

items.statement: No new supply expected in next couple of years, supporting ADR stability.
items.quote: And we don't foresee any new supply coming into the next couple of years as well. So, that way, we are not very concerned by what's happening.

items.statement: Room revenue contributes 55-60% and F&B 35-40% for Marriott and Courtyard; for executive apartments, rooms 64-65% and F&B 32-33%.
items.quote: What I can tell you is, in general, for our Marriott and Courtyard complex, our room revenue contribution is about 55% to 60%, whereas F&B contributes about 35% to 40%. Whilst in the executive apartments, room revenues contribution is about 64% to 65%, and F&B is about 32% to 33%.

items.statement: Sees no impact on ADRs from upcoming supply, as less than half of announced projects may open.
items.quote: So, we see that in no way affecting our ADRs, and our ADRs are still going to be strongly improving because the supply will be less. And second thing, in hotel projects, the planning and the execution and the capital allocation and the time management is very crucial, and the debt management. So, we see, even though a

items.statement: Comfortable with current debt levels and does not anticipate further increases in interest expense.
items.quote: We don't see any further increase. We have healthy cash revenues and healthy cash balances to fund our ongoing renovations.

items.statement: Expects to start paying dividends from next year after completing convention center renovation.
items.quote: So, mostly the board also discussed this issue several times, and we expect to give you a good outcome from next year.

items.statement: Targets 10-15% sales growth for FY27, similar to last four-five years excluding FY26 aberration.
items.quote: So we hope we can continue between 10% to 15% again this year. That's our target.

items.statement: Targets around 12% EBITDA margin for base business in FY27.
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, we are targeting something around that. We are targeting a good sales growth as well, but we have to see how the market reacts.

items.statement: Fill-finish capex estimated at INR50 crores, part of Cefiderocol facility.
items.quote: So the total capex we are estimating is around INR50 crores, which includes equipment and capability but one size.

items.statement: 7ACA project commissioning committed for Q1 CY2027.
items.quote: We are still committed to the commissioning in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Cefiderocol facility commissioning by end of this calendar year; launch expected Q2/Q3 CY2027.
items.quote: The Cefiderocol facility remains on track for commissioning by the end of this calendar year. Subject to regulatory approvals and registrations, we expect product launch during Q2 or Q3 of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Merger with Dhanuka Labs expected to contribute 1-2% EBITDA margin expansion.
items.quote: As these synergies begin getting realized over time, we internally estimate that the merger itself can potentially contribute nearly 1% to 2% EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: 7ACA current price around $61, long-term average $60, fluctuating $55-65.
items.quote: Yes, around $61 is the current price.

items.statement: Growth expected from non-regulated markets, especially Africa and South Asia.
items.quote: And the next growth is probably going to come from Africa and probably South of Asia. So there is definitely growth in Cephalosporin.

items.statement: Pricing increased in April due to war; reviewing prices weekly to pass on rising input costs.
items.quote: So you see the pricing did increase in the month of April, due to the war. People were a little anxious about covering their materials.

items.statement: Regulated market mix was 30% and ROW 70% for FY26.
items.quote: For this year, whole year, 30% is regulated and 70% is ROW.

items.statement: AMS platform remains an annual EBITDA drag of approximately INR8 crores.
items.quote: The platform currently remains an EBITDA drag of approximately INR8 crores annually.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam lifetime sales maintained at $1-2 billion; peak in 4th-5th year of launch.
items.quote: We still maintain the lifetime sales would be between $1 billion to $2 billion overall during the life of the patent.

items.statement: About 30,000 patients treated with Enmetazobactam in the last year.
items.quote: So about 30,000 patients we would have treated in last year.

items.statement: Cyient Semiconductors signed definitive agreement for first external funding of INR300 crores at INR4,650 crores equity valuation from EAAA Alternatives.
items.quote: And today, I'm proud to announce that Cyient Semiconductors has signed a definitive agreement for its first external funding route, a total of INR300 crore s with equity valuation at INR4,650 crores from EAAA Alternatives who were formerly known as Edelweiss Alternatives.

items.statement: Deal structured as INR200 crores debt and INR100 crores equity; rate not disclosed.
items.quote: So, the deal is a combination of debt and equity, debt at 200 crores, equity at 100 crores. It's a competitive rate. We can't disclose the rate because we're still not close to deal.

items.statement: Cyient committed up to $100 million; about $30 million already invested, remaining ~$70 million available.
items.quote: On the funding, Cyient remains committed, like I said, to the $100 million. We've already put in about $30 million. So, rest of the money is available.

items.statement: ASSP gross margin highest at 50-60%, followed by custom ASIC turnkey, then services.
items.quote: From a gross margin standpoint, ASSP given it is product and IP driven will have the highest gross margin typically in the 50% to 60% range, depending on which customer segment you sell, followed by custom ASIC turnkey followed by services.

items.statement: Power ASSP including Kinetic is 50-60% of business; ASSP share to increase over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: So today, Power ASSP s including Kinetic is roughly 50% to 60% of our business. The rest of the business is split between services and ASIC turnkey.

items.statement: Custom ASIC turnkey expected to grow faster than other segments in near term.
items.quote: Now in the near term, we do believe that custom ASIC turnkey will grow faster compared to the other segments. But in the longer term, ASSP will continue to remain a significant portion of our business.

items.statement: ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities, mainly industrial and medical.
items.quote: And finally, commercially, our ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities, and we were selected as the L1 bidder on the SCL semiconductor modernization initiative, one of India's flagship semiconductor programs supported by the government of India.

items.statement: Breakeven still expected late FY27 to early FY28, with possible one-to-two quarter shift.
items.quote: So, for now, we are still looking at a breakeven late FY27, early FY28. But based on the investor conversations, we'll come back.

items.statement: Raised capital to fund R&D, lab infrastructure and working capital for growth roadmap.
items.quote: The capital that we are raising will directly go into R&D, lab infrastructure and working capital to execute on our growth road map.

items.statement: Data center share of power rising from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030; power is biggest data center bottleneck.
items.quote: The share of power for data centers is going up from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030.

items.statement: Power semiconductors addressable market opportunity of approximately $8.5 billion targeted.
items.quote: With our acquisition and internal investment in low- and high-voltage product strategies, we're positioning Cyient semiconductors to participate in the addressable market opportunity of approximately $8.5 billion.

items.statement: Launched 7 new GaN products targeting Indian market, primarily 650-volt; working on 800-volt architecture.
items.quote: In partnership with Navitas as well, we launched 7 new GaN products, specifically targeting the Indian market.

items.statement: Kinetic acquisition completed March 2026 for approximately $85 million, funded by debt at Singapore entity.
items.quote: To accelerate this vision, in March 2026, we completed the acquisition of Kinetic Technologies for approximately $85 million.

items.statement: Semiconductor product R&D development cycle of 2-3 years before commercialization.
items.quote: As we progress and we develop our own products which we are working on, we do believe that ASSP revenue share will increase in the next 3-4 years, because there is an R&D development cycle of almost 2 years to 3 years for the product to commercialize.

items.statement: Reaffirms FY27 top line growth of 15-20%, with potential for stronger growth over coming years.
items.quote: we continue to see robust opportunities across all three product segments in the defines market and therefore reaffirm our FY27 top line growth at 15% to 20% rate, with a potential for much stronger growth over the coming years.

items.statement: Plans FY27 sales of INR1300-1400 crores, 15-20% growth over FY26, with 40% R&D and 60% production.
items.quote: we have planned to book sales of INR1300 crores to INR1400 crores, that is around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26, covering 40% of R&D and 60% from the production area.

items.statement: Expects INR1600+ crores orders bookable in FY27, 25% from R&D and 75% production.
items.quote: Going forward, we have a clear visibility of approximately INR1600 crores plus orders which can be booked in the current year, that is FY27. Around 25% of this expected to come from R&D programs, while balance are basically driven by the production orders.

items.statement: Astra Rafael Comsys (JV) expected to deliver over INR600 crores top line in FY27.
items.quote: It is expected to deliver a top line of over INR600 crores in FY27.

items.statement: ARC expects minimum 50% growth in order booking and sales in FY27; visibility of INR200 crores order book.
items.quote: Going forward in FY27, we expect to outperform and we expect the minimum growth of 50% both in terms of order booking and as well as sales. As on date, we have visibility of INR200 crores order book in FY27 for ARC and also expected to cross INR600 crores sales.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR40-50 crores will continue; no additional capex beyond this for growth.
items.quote: in terms of the capex, as you know every year, we are augmenting the existing requirements by spending close to about INR40 crores, INR50 crores. So that will continue. Therefore, there won't be an additional capex beyond this what we are doing normally.

items.statement: Exports to JV have ~40% gross margin due to higher value addition from co-developed SDR RF portions.
items.quote: Therefore, generally these carry good amount of value add. I would say the gross margin will be close to about 40% kind of thing in these exports.

items.statement: Current year margins at 55%; expects to sustain current margins, not improve further.
items.quote: See, the margins delivered by the company in the current year is about 55%. Okay? So, you are still expecting an improvement over 50%-55%? Look at the industry standards. Yes, as we move forward, definitely there will be a change in the product mix of the company, but again it is subjected to various other variables. W

items.statement: Exited low-margin build-to-print business; new exports have ~45% margins vs single-digit in BTP.
items.quote: So here although it is BTP, but our value addition is more and the margins as Mr. SGR had already mentioned, it is around 45% as compared to the single-digit figure in the BTP business.

items.statement: Total addressable market of INR28,000 crores shifted from FY26-FY28 to FY28-FY31 due to program delays.
items.quote: the overall accessible market remains same, but only thing is we instead of FY28-FY29 may go up to FY30-FY31.

items.statement: Aims to triple turnover over 4.5-5.5 years, driven by 5-6 major programs; rear-ended growth.
items.quote: We are expecting at least next, down the line three to four years to triple the revenue or maybe you can say up to FY30 to FY31.

items.statement: Space margins better than defence, but space is only 10-15% of sales; order book reduction won't hurt overall margins.
items.quote: Definitely the space margins are better compared to even defence also, but when you look at the overall space sales contribution, in the overall sales of the company, it is just around 10% to 15% kind of thing. Therefore, the reduction in the space order book or overall space contribution to the sales of the company sh

items.statement: Group revenue expected to grow double-digit in FY27.
items.quote: Firstly, from a group revenue standpoint, we see and expect a double-digit growth this year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 12-13.5% for FY27, including SCS.
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA, we are guiding for a 12 % to 13.5% range for the year. And this is inclusive of SCS, which will now be part of the (GCM ) Global Cables and Mechatronics Division.

items.statement: GCM EBITDA margin expected to improve to 10-12% in FY27 from 6% last year.
items.quote: GCM as a consolidated division last year, if you consider SCS part of it, it was at 6%. And we are expecting that this year to the EBITDA margin to be 10% to 12%.

items.statement: FY27 capex allocated INR 200 crores for land, STC building, Chennai plant, SCD expansion.
items.quote: We have a CAPEX allocated for about INR 200 crores. This is covering AURIC Maharashtra land purchase, STC building completion, SAL Chennai Plant -2, and the SCD capacity expansion.

items.statement: India ICM division expects double-digit revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins in FY27.
items.quote: We again see double -digit growth here, despite the single -digit sector outlook. This is mainly going to be driven by gains in market share and Beyond Cable project ramp ups that we have already won.

items.statement: SCD division expects another year of double-digit growth with EBITDA margins in line with FY26.
items.quote: SCD will have another strong year of double-digit growth. EBITDA margins should continue to be in line with FY26.

items.statement: Company will push customers to pass on increased commodity costs; most expected to be passed on.
items.quote: But we will be pushing our customers for compensation for commodity prices, which have increased. And unless the Middle East crisis comes to an end pretty soon, it will further increase.

items.statement: FY27 forecasts subject to Middle East situation, commodity impact, supply chain stability, and customer launch timing changes.
items.quote: Firstly, needless to say, these forecasts are subject to many changes and the Middle East situation and the commodity impact it may cause the supply chain stability globally and some customer launch timings changing as per what they have given us as a schedule.

items.statement: Global division has strong order book, especially India and China, both double-digit; SAL planning Chennai expansion.
items.quote: Our global division has also got a strong order book, especially in India and China, where both India and China are a double digit. And our India operation, which is SC L, is now planning an expansion in Chennai to cater to the growth.

items.statement: Electronics division momentum in digital clusters and electronic throttle controls expected to carry into FY27.
items.quote: And overall, if you look at it, what happened in SED is that we got a significant business momentum in digital clusters and electronic throttle controls. And this is expected to be carried over into FY27 also.

items.statement: Tariff recoveries from customers and government expected to fully resolve within next few months.
items.quote: On the tariff side, I think both from the customers and from the government, the recoveries are ongoing. We expect a full resolution for all the tariff -related matters, hopefully within the next few months.

items.statement: Largest halogen lamp manufacturer's insolvency driving new customer discussions for low-cost India manufacturing.
items.quote: The insolvency means there are a lot of active discussions now underway with multiple new customers who are looking to utilize our low-cost manufacturing in India.

items.statement: SCS will no longer be separately disclosed; combined under GCM from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Finally, as disclosed, SCS will no longer be separately disclosed. So, that will be part of GCM. We will be combining it under the Global Cables and Mechatronics division from Q1 at FY 27.

items.statement: Expects global SCD/SCS margin to improve to 10-12% from 6-7% last fiscal, driven by restructuring.
items.quote: But it is significantly the restructuring that we have done not only at SCS, but within the Controls division is what is bringing that margin up by as you rightly say, from last year 6% to 10%-12% is what we have guided.

items.statement: Mexico tariffs of $1-2 million absorbed in material cost will permanently continue, including FY27-28.
items.quote: No, What I am saying, where we could not pass on is maybe between $ 1 million to $2 million, which we absorbed, that will be permanently will be there in our material cost itself.

items.statement: Potential $6 million recovery from US Federal Government 301 tariff case expected in 3-6 months; not in margin guidance.
items.quote: That $6 million is still an ongoing tussle between us and the Federal Government. We are in the final stages of coming to a resolution by the Court , which I am hopeful that in the next three to six months, we will hear from.

items.statement: Tariff duty refunds from US government expected in 3-6 months, but much must be passed back to customers.
items.quote: And eventually, hopefully, in the next three to six months’ time, some of the duties will come. So, we have an issue of timing in terms of recovery of these duties.

items.statement: Aims for at least 20% share of business from largest global EV customer in China within 2-3 years.
items.quote: I would say over a period of time, I think maybe in China, at least if we do not get, let us say, 20% of that customer’s share of business in the next two, three years’ time, maybe we would think that we have not been very successful.

items.statement: US non-automotive demand recovery remains slow and tepid, in line with global trends.
items.quote: The recovery of this non-automotive side of the business in US is still slow. There are two parts to it. Some of them have got relocated to smaller handheld grass cutters, etc., relocated to China, most of it. But generally, the business growth has been very tepid still.

items.statement: TRIFA brand lost about $3 million in business due to Middle East market issues.
items.quote: Maybe about $3 million probably because of the loss of business of TRIFA brand.

items.statement: New medium-force actuators developed by tech center; samples to customers in coming months, business in 1-2 years.
items.quote: And we are expecting to have samples of those now with a lot of our customers in the coming few months, where we have redesigned an actuator for having a lower force and of course, in terms of cost and quietness for the cabin, we have tried to develop an actuator that is better than our competition.

items.statement: Motors sourcing shifted from China to Indian supplier, eliminating tariff risk on motors.
items.quote: It was shifted to an Indian supplier, that is now what is going on. So, that had helped us in reducing the tariff risks and now the tariff risk is completely off because our customer assembles with our motors, which is in India origin

items.statement: Employee cost ratio expected to improve this year due to restructuring, driving margin improvement.
items.quote: I would expect that by this year’s number should be an improvement. One of the reasons why we are saying there is an improvement in margin is not because the material costs will change. What is changing is the employee cost and other expenses because of the restructuring.

items.statement: Expects double-digit business growth in global business despite flat underlying automotive market.
items.quote: And that’s why when I said we are talking about double digit business growth in global business, when there is a global business underlying automotive or whatever the business is actually not growing, says that somebody else is suffering in the process.

items.statement: Phoenix Lamps renamed to include electricals; launched horns, more products expected in coming months.
items.quote: As a first step, as you probably may be knowing that we launched our horns as a part of our internally manufactured product into the market, it is a first step. I think hopefully in the months to come, you will hear more from us on other products and projects that you will be able to do at the PLE.

items.statement: SAL-2 plant in Chennai/Vallam is purely capacity expansion as SAL is running out of capacity.
items.quote: Now, coming to the SAL part of the question on SAL -2, that is purely capacity building because we are running out of capacity in terms of physical infrastructure building, etc. Therefore, we have to have an SAL-2.

items.statement: FY27 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore, gradually rising to INR1,600 crore.
items.quote: FY27, it will be like about INR1,400 crores to INR 1,500 crores and then gradually inch up to INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: No new capex planned; remaining capex of INR125 crore to be spent in FY27.
items.quote: After this round of capex, we are not really foreseeing any other capex or any kind of investment happening.

items.statement: AI and digital initiatives expected to reduce total manufacturing cost by 5-8%.
items.quote: we look forward at around 5% to 8% of total cost of manufacturing coming down from the existing levels.

items.statement: Targeting specialty papers to be 25-30% of total capacity.
items.quote: we are going to look at having about 25% to 30% of our entire capacity sort of catering to specialty needs.

items.statement: Current NSR stable at INR69,000-70,000 per ton.
items.quote: we are being able to maintain our pricing at a healthy level of about between INR69,000 and INR70,000 per ton, and it's working well and stable for us.

items.statement: Wheat straw prices up 50-60% YoY, expected to fall with rice sowing season.
items.quote: Wheat straw pricing is higher by about 50%, 60% compared to last year in a similar period.

items.statement: Chemical input costs rose 3-5%; difficult to pass on currently.
items.quote: the input chemical cost has risen in some chemicals, not all by around 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Lean season next 2-3 months; pricing recovery expected around September.
items.quote: this is a lean season, the next 2, 3 months. And historically also, we see dampening in pricing.

items.statement: West Asia crisis may divert Chinese/Indonesian paper exports to India at predatory pricing.
items.quote: the West Asia crisis has also created the risk of trade diversion with export-oriented paper producers from China and Indonesia potentially redirecting surplus inventories to India at predatory pricing

items.statement: Open to low-cost capital options like rights/QIP to reduce interest burden.
items.quote: We are looking at various options. We will certainly take your advice and take note of what you're saying. And we will look at alternate options of how to get in low costing capital into the company

items.statement: Existing dealer network of ~90 dealers plus 20 more can absorb additional capacity.
items.quote: We have about 90-odd dealers who are committed to us and the offtakes are very regular.

items.statement: Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by financial year-end.
items.quote: we've also submitted an anti-subsidy application, which works faster. And we are expecting that to be processed and come to fruition by, let's say, this year-end or by this financial year-end.

items.statement: Order book target at least 3x revenues; currently over 4x, giving robust revenue visibility.
items.quote: We said we will k eep our order book at least 3x of revenues. We are at over 4x of revenues, giving a robust revenue visibility.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR guidance of 15% to 20%; this year achieved almost 20%, the higher end of band.
items.quote: 15% to 20% CAGR of revenue, this year we did almost 20% on the higher side of the band.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance band of 13% to 15%; company has firmly remained within it for 2-3 years.
items.quote: EBITDA 13% to 15%, we've firmly remained in that band not just this year, but over the last 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: ROCE target over 20%; currently near 20% and expected to cross in next couple of years.
items.quote: ROCE over 20% we are getting closer to that and I'm sure in the next couple of years we wi ll surely cross 20%.

items.statement: O&M share targeted to rise from 17% to 20% under medium-term 3-5 year outlook.
items.quote: O&M at 17% we said that our medium-term 3 to 5-year outlook is to take it to 20% and we are working and on track from that perspective.

items.statement: ROE target over 15%; currently closer to 16% and inching upwards.
items.quote: ROE over 15% we are closer to 16% now, inching upwards, profitability, better returns a nd net cash positive for the sixth consecutive year.

items.statement: Order intake closed at INR 7,500 crore versus INR 5,700 crore last year; order book INR 17,200 crore.
items.quote: Our order intake we closed with INR 7,500 crore almost that is year-over-year. Last year we did about INR 5,700 crore this year we have done INR 7,500 crore and closed with an order book of INR 17,200 crore

items.statement: Order backlog grew 26% year-over-year, faster than 20% revenue growth, improving forward visibility.
items.quote: Year-over-year, our order backlog grew by 26%. When our revenue grew by 20%, we have grown our order backlog by 26%.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 5 per share, up from INR 4 last year.
items.quote: the board recommended a final dividend of INR 5/- per share, up from INR 4/- last year, recommended to the shareholders for approval.

items.statement: GCC market seen at about USD 5 billion per year of opportunity over next 10 years.
items.quote: For the next 10 years, we see an average of $5 billion per year of opportunity.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in Gulf, government spending cuts, and currency/raw material volatility flagged as headwinds.
items.quote: When you see the headwinds, we are seeing recently the geopolitical situation in Gulf area, which is trying to affect the smooth operations of this market.

items.statement: Company avoids state/municipality-funded projects, citing payment security as biggest selection factor.
items.quote: We don't take projects which are funded by state government or municipalities because we consider that as a big risk.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 950 crore, sixth consecutive year and thirteenth consecutive quarter net cash positive.
items.quote: We closed the year as net cash positive for sixth consecutive year and thirteenth consecutive quarter.

items.statement: Management maintains 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA margin guardrails, with new strategy to be shared later.
items.quote: But broadly the guardrails remain, that we will grow at a 15% to 20%, continue to grow profitably. Our EBITDA margins will remain 13% to 15%.

items.statement: International revenue mix to increase from current 50%, improving margins and working capital.
items.quote: Today we are at 50 % and 50%, we're looking at Middle East, Africa, you've seen the sizes that are there, so this will provide an opportunity for better margins as well as better working capital profiles.

items.statement: Medium-long term objective to take O&M share to 20% of business.
items.quote: And third is, of course, our medium-long term objective of taking O&M to 20%.

items.statement: Kuwait order expected next month; Saudi order may slip to next quarter.
items.quote: It's very imminent the one from Kuwait should happen I think next month. Within this quarter we can get that. And the Saudi one may go to the next quarter.

items.statement: Company remains asset-light, no investment in real assets, equipment, or manufacturing.
items.quote: We don't invest in equi pment; we don't invest in manufacturing. We are a design technology company, which is all brain here.

items.statement: Price variation clauses cover 70% of costs in large Indian long-duration projects; international projects generally lack such clauses.
items.quote: But in most of the large Indian orders, we have a price variation clause where we are covered by any fluctuation which happens. But still, it only covers 70% of our costs, not 100% of the cost.

items.statement: Middle East disturbances and Eid may delay order finalizations.
items.quote: And being in Middle East, especially with the disturbed conditions there, plus Eid is coming. So all those things have some disturbances, but I don't think we have to wait too long.

items.statement: Company is open to bolt-on acquisitions for technology globally.
items.quote: Definitely. Short answer is yes.

items.statement: Municipal platform update expected next quarter; company remains asset-light.
items.quote: I think I have to wait for another quarter to bring that kind of information or news to you.

items.statement: AI partnership with Pani Energy showing positive KPIs; plans to expand to other plants.
items.quote: So there is an expectation or what we are realizing: reduced chemical consumption, better utilization of water. There are very many other parameters on which result is positive, we are enthused.

items.statement: Bio-CNG plant to serve 3,500 homes or 400 vehicles daily; not very lucrative but scalable.
items.quote: The volume what we are going to generate is going to serve per day around 3,500 homes can get their cooking gas or 400 vehicles.

items.statement: India market opening up in industrial and municipal segments; recent order wins to drive revenue.
items.quote: Now with the market opening up here both on industrial and municipal, you're already seeing us booking a lot of orders.

items.statement: No diversification outside water planned; water market offers sufficient growth opportunities.
items.quote: I think one thing I want to clarify as of now, th ere is no need, and we are not looking at in the near future of any diversification which is outside water.

items.statement: Company invests annually in R&D for technology upgrades; patents and trademarks growing.
items.quote: So we are investing every year and that's how you see our patents and trademarks which are developing every year, though some of the old patents will expire but we quickly have new patents.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped about 1.5-1.6% in FY26, largely due to commodity cost impact and revenue mix.
items.quote: Coming to the gross margin, the gross margin, when you look at, it's slightly dropped. If you look at in terms of margin, it is close to 1.6%, 1.5% drop.

items.statement: Copper and aluminum rose over 30% and steel about 10% between April 2025 and March 2026.
items.quote: Just to give you like copper, aluminum in last 1 year, I'm talking about the year, which is between April '25 and March '26, has seen an upward movement of 30% plus.

items.statement: Commodity hedging covers 50-60% of exposure; forex hedged via PO-level and net ARAP hedging.
items.quote: So commodity hedging is completely covered up to the 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Large infrastructure projects over 6-month delivery include variable contract clauses to recover price increases from customers.
items.quote: Mostly what we try to do the large infrastructure project, which is more than 6-month delivery period, which always with the customer with some variable contract.

items.statement: Data centers currently represent about 10-12% of order backlog and are expected to increase.
items.quote: Maybe if under control of my CFO, maybe typically about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Management hopes deferred deliveries recover in Q1 FY27, contingent on LPG and copper issues resolving.
items.quote: So I hope that will recover in Q1.

items.statement: Service revenue mix shifted toward lower-margin modernization/revamp projects versus spares and AMC.
items.quote: Other 2 has better margin than third one, which is modernization and RA.

items.statement: New dry-type Trihal transformer to be made in Baroda, targeting data centers, metros, commercial buildings, hospitals.
items.quote: And that is what we are going to bring in Baroda, and we will start catering to especially areas like data centers.

items.statement: Q4 order intake was selective due to commodity uncertainty; company prioritized orders with price variability clauses.
items.quote: The Q4 order intake because of uncertainty in commodity market, we were very, very selective.

items.statement: Company is setting up a skill center in North India with PFC to train DISCOM personnel on grid management.
items.quote: And we are also in process of setting up one of the such skill center in North India to -- which will be used by PFC to train people.

items.statement: Confident of at least 10-12% revenue growth in current year, possibly more.
items.quote: 10%, 12% is the bare minimum we should be hitting, and we are confident of doing that for this year.

items.statement: Aims to return to pre-investment EBITDA margin profile of 14-15%.
items.quote: I think we would like to go back to the EBITDA margins that we were at before all of this and before our investments and everything.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget of INR10-15 crores, including maintenance and new machinery.
items.quote: for the current year, we have a budget of around INR10 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: Plans to pay off most debt in next 4 years, reducing finance cost.
items.quote: we can pay most of the debt in next 4 years.

items.statement: Expects domestic revenue growth to outpace exports in FY27.
items.quote: in terms of revenue growth, we are expecting more from the domestic market than from the export market.

items.statement: Domestic price list revised twice last quarter to pass on costs; some lag remains.
items.quote: in the last quarter, we've revised our price list twice to be able to pass on the prices.

items.statement: Unable to immediately pass on price increases in Europe and US due to weak demand.
items.quote: Europe being one of our largest marks, we were not able to immediately pass on the price.

items.statement: Domestic demand drivers include formalization, stricter BIS, and worker awareness.
items.quote: the formalization of the wage code, that should help having more of MNCs setup shops in the country

items.statement: New PU gloves and PVC gumboots target import substitution and export markets.
items.quote: India imports roughly around anywhere between INR80 crores to INR90 crores of these gloves

items.statement: US TAA list excludes India, making it challenging to gain US customers.
items.quote: India is one of the countries which is outside this list.

items.statement: Sanand facility running at 50% capacity, targeting INR40 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: we are running at around 50% capacity, and we are trying to improve it gradually.

items.statement: Eligible for INR10 crores capital subsidy for Sanand project, applying this year.
items.quote: as per tax side policy there in the range of INR10 crores, we should be getting.

items.statement: India branded generic growth to be 100-150 bps above market, implying double-digit growth.
items.quote: I have always maintained that we will grow 100 to 150 basis points higher than the market.

items.statement: U.S. pharma growth expected high single-digit in dollar terms, plus forex gains and new launches.
items.quote: U.S. market from a currency-to-currency basis, the dollar to dollar, we are looking at a high single -digit margin and the currency gain would add up to that.

items.statement: ROW markets expected to grow in higher teens.
items.quote: From the ROW markets, we have looked at a higher teen’s kind of growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected 20-21% in FY27, similar to FY26, with geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: In the current scenario, we have touched a 20.4% kind of growth like-to-like, we would -- we should be within the range of 20% to 21%.

items.statement: Tax rate guidance revised to 27-29% from 35-38% due to new tax regime.
items.quote: So, we want to revise our guidance on tax rate. The number will be around 27% to 29% going forward.

items.statement: API and packaging material prices increasing; impact expected in Q1 and beyond if situation persists.
items.quote: Definitely, there is an impact on first quarter. There will be impact going forward also if the situation doesn’t improve from here.

items.statement: No further acquisitions for next 12 months; focus on integrating Occlutech.
items.quote: we don't foresee any further investment into acquisitions at least for the next 12 months.

items.statement: Dividend payout to increase as percentage of PAT due to higher tax rate, but absolute dividend maintained.
items.quote: if we maintain the same absolute value, then definitely the payout percentage will go up. But we don't foresee any major reduction in absolute value of d ividend.

items.statement: Chronic share of branded generic business at 22%, improving by at least 1% annually.
items.quote: today, our chronic business as far as branded generic business is concerned. We are close to 22% of our business is from chronic and which is if you see our last 3- or 4-years trend, every year, we are improving it internally by at least 1%.

items.statement: Geopolitical environment and supply chain dynamics may cause near-term headwinds.
items.quote: These external factors may lead to some near-term headwinds.

items.statement: Semaglutide launch achieved 11% unit market share; expected to increase.
items.quote: we could garner a market -- unit market share of around 11% and we expect it to go up even further in the coming months.

items.statement: Occlutech acquisition expected to close in 45-60 days; full impact from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: when the deal will close maybe in like in 45 to 60 days.

items.statement: Tolvaptan launch expected September-October 2026, contributing in H2 FY27.
items.quote: our expected launch is around September or October, somewhere around that time.

items.statement: R&D expenses expected 4-5% of revenue in FY27.
items.quote: we expect it to be similar between 4% to 5% even in the coming year.

items.statement: No specific FY27 guidance given, but management expects FY27 to be a better year after difficult FY26.
items.quote: So, Mr. Varun, again for next year we are not giving any specific number on the guidance part. But whatever has happened in last two years, we were obviously in a difficult situation

items.statement: New capex at existing plant postponed and kept on hold.
items.quote: we had guided to say that we will do some sort of capex but that as was previously mentioned in our board meeting that we are postponing the newer capex which we are supposed to do in our existing plant. So, that we are keeping it on hold.

items.statement: Patent product portfolio increased from 30% to 40% of branded sales.
items.quote: So, presently our patent product portfolio has gone up from 30% to 40% of our branded, which almost entire formulation everything is done in our own factory.

items.statement: Ideal EBITDA margin: branded 18-20%, B2B around 8%.
items.quote: For example this year our sales were little lower but if I have to tell you on the ideal situation that next year if we are going to perform well and based on that sales number the EBITDA margin for the branded should be anywhere from 18-20% and on the B2B it should be around 8% or so.

items.statement: Branded gross margin around 40%, B2B 15-20%.
items.quote: For branded depending upon product but since our portfolio of patent is going up, we are on an average at around 40% whereas on the B2B we are at around 15-20%.

items.statement: El Nino expected to kick in September-October, potentially impacting Rabi season; company adjusting business accordingly.
items.quote: We do know that the probability of the El Nino becoming significant is 4th October where potentially there will be a 2 degree plus increase in the El Nino and this would impact the Rabi season. So, we are appropriately trying to be able to adjust our business to be able to take this into account.

items.statement: Introducing five new biostimulant products for FY27.
items.quote: Currently, we have introduced five new products for FY26-27.

items.statement: FY27 will see launches of Fluzam, Midcotin, Cubax Power Extra, and Trishanku patented products.
items.quote: FY’27 will see us launch Fluzam, Midcotin, Cubax Power Extra, and Trishanku. These patented products are expected to further strengthen our positioning in the specialized crop protection market.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from ₹958 crore in FY24 to ₹651 crore as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: I am pleased to share that inventory levels have reduced significantly from approximately ₹958 crore in FY24 to ₹773 crore in FY25 and further to ₹651 crore as of March 31, 2026.

items.statement: May take additional government-backed 20% funding; already applied to banks.
items.quote: So, for the liquidity even the government is helping with respect to 20% additional funding so we might take some portion of it. We have already applied to the banks.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target around INR400 crores with 14% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: No, we are targeting a turnover of around INR400 crores and an EBITDA margin of 14% at present.

items.statement: Expects 50 basis point improvement in gross margin.
items.quote: I think we can expect another 50-basis point improvement in gross margin.

items.statement: Gross margin to remain around 49% to 50% with new season products.
items.quote: So you'll see that the gross margin remains more or less in the upper side of around 49% to 50%.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased 20-25%; MRP increased by INR25-50 in retail.
items.quote: The raw material prices are increased around 20% to 25% compared to -- in the month of February to now. But still, we have also increased our MRP and trying to remain competitive and again, don't reduce the gross margin.

items.statement: Athleisure limited due to small store size; will not expand further.
items.quote: So we'll keep the athleisure to the extent it is required, but we will not go far-fetched in athleisure.

items.statement: Demand weakness and political turmoil are key risks to FY27 guidance.
items.quote: There are risks like -- demand weakness is a risk, then some risk comes in the political turmoil, all these are there.

items.statement: Inventory correction done; will increase inventory for new season.
items.quote: Already, the inventory correction has been done. Now this year, we'll increase the inventory to the extent that is needed.

items.statement: Target steady state store count around 200 COCO stores.
items.quote: Around 200 COCO stores.

items.statement: E-commerce contribution around 5%; expect higher this year.
items.quote: Around 5%, but we are focusing now more on e-commerce, especially on our khadim.com. This year, we are expecting the contribution will be higher than last year.

items.statement: Net debt target INR110-115 crores post restructuring.
items.quote: INR110 crores to INR115 crores.

items.statement: Lost INR10-15 crores sales in last two quarters due to inventory reduction.
items.quote: For stock thing, maybe around INR10 crores to INR15 crores of sales we have lost for the last 2 quarters.

items.statement: PAT margin aspiration 2-2.5% if sales grow.
items.quote: If the sales grows, we will be able to have PAT of around 2% to 2.5% that we used to do earlier.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach Rs. 25 crores by end of June.
items.quote: However, by the end of June, we are expecting that our order book should come to somewhere around Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: Current order book at beginning of financial year was Rs. 10 crores.
items.quote: As of the beginning of the financial year, we had around Rs. 10 crores of order book in hand.

items.statement: Bids participated approximately Rs. 15 crores in value.
items.quote: And as far as the number of bids that we have right now participated in are concerned, they are approximately Rs. 15 crores in value.

items.statement: Flagship BTS 2000 product enjoys average margins of 35-40%.
items.quote: However, from a target point of view, when I'm talking about our flagship product, BTS 2000, average margins are somewhere around 35% to 40 %.

items.statement: Net margins taper to 10-15% due to competitive products.
items.quote: Obviously, that tapers down to a net of 10 -15% because of other more competitive products.

items.statement: Export revenue expected to be around 10% of total revenues this year.
items.quote: In this year, if I have to talk about the export percentage, vis-a-vis the total revenues, it would be somewhere around 10&, still 90% of it we are focusing from the domestic markets.

items.statement: Market potential for Aartech estimated at Rs. 50-100 crores.
items.quote: But yes, broadly, I can say that for Aartech, and to serve its customers with the kind of size Aartech has right now, the market potential looks somewhere around 50 to 100 crores.

items.statement: Organic growth rate of 12-15% per year expected to continue.
items.quote: In five years, we can see that we have actually doubled ourselves, and it is progressively growing on an organic rate of around 12 to 15 percent every year.

items.statement: New Narmadapuram facility commercial operations targeted by end FY27 or early FY28.
items.quote: And as I just mentioned, that commercial operations are targeted by the end of 26-27 or early 27-28.

items.statement: Civil and infrastructure work at new facility expected to complete in 9-10 months.
items.quote: The civil and infrastructure work is underway, and we are expecting that that should be done in the next nine to ten months.

items.statement: Defence sector seen as high growth with good margins but high entry barriers.
items.quote: Today, when we are sitting here, we all see that defence is one of the most sunrise sectors. And because a lot of emphasis is being given by our government for “Make in India”, definitely this sector looks very, very good in terms of, or potentially good, in terms of revenues and margins.

items.statement: Export markets unpredictable due to geopolitical situations.
items.quote: So, sir, to actually understand the export markets and with the current geopolitical situations, it's very unpredictable.

items.statement: Patent for Adaptive Alternative Power Module expected in 12-18 months.
items.quote: There is also a patent that we have filed for this particular product under the civil -military collaboration, and we are expecting it in the next 12 to 18 months for the patent to come in our books.

items.statement: Steady returns of 5-10% per year focused for investors.
items.quote: And we have focused to give steady returns of around, between 5% to 10% every year.

items.statement: GFL earmarks INR 3,150 crores capex for FY27, with INR 2,300 crores for GFCL EV and INR 850 crores for GFL.
items.quote: GFL has earmarked INR 3,150 crores of capex for FY '27, of which INR2,300 is for GFCL EV and INR850 crores for GFL.

items.statement: Battery materials capex of INR 2,300 crores planned for FY27, part of INR 6,000 crores cumulative by FY28.
items.quote: To support this growth road map, we have planned a c apex of approximately INR2,300 crores for FY '27 across the battery materials portfolio, largely focused on growth capex, including the anode active material project.

items.statement: Fluoropolymers expected to grow 15-20% in FY27 versus last year.
items.quote: So this year, we expect to see a growth of around 15% to 20% as compared to the last year in our fluoropolymers products, which we are going ahead.

items.statement: Battery materials revenue to reach 3-digit number by Q4 FY27, with significant QoQ growth.
items.quote: And we expect to reach, of course, the 3- digit number by the end of this quarter -- by the end of this financial year in the last quarter, yes.

items.statement: GFL's INR 850 crores FY27 capex breakdown: INR 150 crores refrigerants, INR 222 crores electronic chemicals, INR 250 crores fluoropolymers, INR 230 crores backward integration.
items.quote: Of INR850 crores c apex, approximately INR 150 crores will be spent on expanding our refrigerant gas and related infrastructure capacities.
