items.statement: INR 150 crores capex for refrigerant gas capacity expansion in FY27.
items.quote: We will be incurring INR 150 crores of c apex on increasing capacities of refrigerant gases in the current financial year.

items.statement: All initial battery materials capacities under phase one are commissioned and contracted.
items.quote: Against this backdrop, we are pleased to s hare that all the initial capacities planned under phase one have now been commissioned and contracted for.

items.statement: LiPF6 salt has orders for FY27 and beyond, with production ramping up quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: We have orders in place for FY '27 and beyond. Accordingly, producti on will be ramped up quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Battery materials targeted EBITDA margins over 25% plus, with asset turns of nearly 2x.
items.quote: To support this growth road map, we remain committed to our previously outlined guidelines of INR6,000 crores cumulative capex by FY '28 across the battery materials portfolio, with targeted asset turns of ne arly 2x and EBITDA margins of over 25% plus.

items.statement: GFL has taken price increases in fluoropolymers, similar to competitors, to offset raw material and logistics cost rises.
items.quote: There has been a price increase. We have also taken a price increase and because if you look at it, that we have been, in spite of increasing raw materials and the logistics prices, we have been able to maintain our EBITDA margins and continue to show growth in our business.

items.statement: Refrigerant demand expected to remain healthy, driven by air conditioning, refrigeration, cold chain, and AI data center cooling.
items.quote: Demand for refrigerants is expected to remain healthy, supported by increasing penetration of residential air conditioning, commercial refrigeration, cold chain infrastructures and surge in demand of cooling infrastructure for AI data centers across the globe.

items.statement: Caustic soda demand outlook stable in FY27, but pricing likely range-bound due to domestic capacity additions.
items.quote: Within bulk chemicals, the demand outlook for caustic soda is expected to remain stable in FY '27. While pricing is likely to remain range-bound due to domestic capacity additions and balanced supply/demand dynamics.

items.statement: New fluoropolymer capacities to be added, focusing on high-value products like PFA and FKM.
items.quote: And going ahead in the new fluoropolymers business, especially PFA, FKM and a couple of other products which we have added, we are seeing that the growth is continuing, and that is why our c apex is also being planned.

items.statement: Oman capex to proceed despite Middle East situation; Oman considered safe with no impact on plans.
items.quote: We will go ahead with the c apex, There are no impacts on Oman, if you look at the overall capacity. Oman has been overall one of the safest countries so far in the Middle East. And so there's no change in our capex plan and we are going ahead with it.

items.statement: Board approved additional Rs 2,000 crore investment for greenfield large power transformer facility in Karjan, Gujarat, to be completed by Q4 CY2028.
items.quote: During our Q4FY26 Board Meeting, the Board approved an additional investment of Rs. 2,000 Crores. This includes among other initiatives, the establishment of greenfield large power transformer facility in Karjan, Vadodara in Gujarat.

items.statement: Total cumulative capex now close to Rs 4,000 crore, including previously announced Rs 2,000 crore from October 2024.
items.quote: With this, our total cumulative capex stands close to Rs. 4,000 Crores.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin was 15.4%, up from 9.3% last year.
items.quote: EBITDA margin on an annualized basis is 15.4%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operational EBITDA margin was 16.4%.
items.quote: Operational EBITDA for this quarter was Rs. 452.3 Crores, which is 16.4%.

items.statement: Most portfolio has commodity price pass-through and price variation clauses to protect margins amid inflation.
items.quote: But most of our portfolio, we have commodity price pass-through. We have a price variation clause built in, in the contracts, and we openly and transparently do that.

items.statement: Demand outlook remains robust supported by energy transition, grid expansion, and increasing electrification.
items.quote: Looking ahead, the demand outlook remains robust supported by energy transition, grid expansion and increasing electrification.

items.statement: Data center market in India expected to grow 6-9x from less than 2 GW to 13-18 GW, with Hitachi Energy addressing 15% of capex.
items.quote: Looking at the data center market in India, which we are primarily catering to is less than 2 gigawatts. And the projections are anywhere between 13 to 18 gigawatts depending upon which data.

items.statement: HVDC revenues were around Rs 1,100 crore out of total Rs 8,000 crore in FY26, about 15%.
items.quote: If you take the whole of this year, our HVDC revenues out of Rs. 8,000 Crores is around Rs. 1,100 Crores or something like that, Ajay?

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in Middle East causing supply chain pressure; mitigation measures in place.
items.quote: The current geopolitical situation in the Middle East has triggered pressure on the supply chains. However, we have put several mitigation measures to address the temporary challenges which not only we are facing it, but the whole industry is facing.

items.statement: New transformer capacity will add 30-40 GVA, doubling existing capacity.
items.quote: We are going to create anywhere between 30 GVA to 40 GVA, exactly close to our existing factory.

items.statement: Exports average around 25-30% of revenue and orders, excluding large HVDC orders.
items.quote: So, export revenue, if you see year-end is around 25%, you can take -- and orders also will be basically in the similar line. Currently, we look a little bit lower because we have booked large domestic orders, but our average exports are around 25% to 30%.

items.statement: HVDC pipeline robust with 3-4 projects expected in next 2 years, combination of LCC and VSC.
items.quote: And similarly, there are many other projects, what I understand is also in the pipeline, at least in the next 2 years, we are talking about anywhere between 3 projects, if not, 4.

items.statement: Commissioned India's first city infeed project in Mumbai, 1,000 MW VSC-based HVDC.
items.quote: I just talked about Mumbai City infeed project of 1,000 megawatt on a VSC-based technology.

items.statement: Entire capex program to be fully commissioned in H1 FY27.
items.quote: We expect the entire capex program to be fully commissioned during the first half of the current financial year.

items.statement: FY27 PAT likely to remain at a relatively moderate level.
items.quote: For FY'27 PAT is likely to remain at a relatively moderate level.

items.statement: Expect initial benefits from new capacities to start reflecting from current financial year.
items.quote: we expect the initial benefits to start reflecting from the current financial year itself through higher volumes, improved product availability and incremental revenue contribution.

items.statement: Expect stronger revenue growth and improved profitability over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: we expect stronger revenue growth, which will subsequently translate into improved profitability.

items.statement: No major capex; only maintenance capex of approx INR20 crore in FY27.
items.quote: There is no additional capex plan. Whatever capex is pending and whatever CWIP is there, we are just completing that. Apart from that, some maintenance and some required commercial viable capex will be there. Otherwise, no major capex.

items.statement: Gross margin should not go below 65%.
items.quote: we believe that the margin should not go below 65%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins should be similar to Q4, not worse.
items.quote: It shouldn't be worse, but should be in similar regions.

items.statement: Gradually increasing prices due to 60-70% raw material cost hike; may not pass on entire increase.
items.quote: we are looking to gradually increase pricing because at 60% or 70% raw material price hikes, it is a large cost increase, and we would not be able to support such a large cost increase by absorbing it.

items.statement: Domestic market favorable for last 6-7 months; expect good stable growth over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: we expect good growth from the domestic market, strong stable growth from the domestic market over the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: International growth could be significantly higher than domestic over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: internationally, I think the growth numbers could be much higher, significantly higher than domestic the growth percentages

items.statement: Cell culture to ramp up slowly; significant momentum from FY28.
items.quote: I think we should see some significant momentum towards year 2 and moving forward, year 2, 3 and 4 should be able to really help us scale up the volumes

items.statement: Raw material price spike of 70% from normalized levels due to Middle East conflict.
items.quote: you see raw material price increases as much as 70% from normalized levels.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions impacted exports; some easing observed.
items.quote: we have observed some easing of supply chain-related issues over the past 2 weeks.

items.statement: Focus on deleveraging; debt not to exceed 2x EBITDA.
items.quote: I would ideally in a situation -- in an ideal situation, not want debt to increase more than 2x our EBITDA.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target approximately INR 670 crores, ~40% YoY growth.
items.quote: For FY27, as Suresh was mentioning, the company is targeting a revenue of approximately INR670 crores, reflecting a growth of around 40% year-on-year, along with a projected PAT of INR144 crores for the next year.

items.statement: FY27 PAT target over INR 144 crores.
items.quote: For FY27, we are targeting revenues of approximately INR 670 crores with a profit after tax of over INR144 crores and with continued improvement growth supported by operating leverage, restructuring benefits and as always, disciplined execution across all our businesses.

items.statement: Commerce business targeting INR 1,000+ crores revenue by FY30.
items.quote: Post demerger, the Commerce business is targeting significant scale up through product and geographic expansion over the next few years with a long-term aspiration of achieving INR 1,000 crores plus revenue by FY30.

items.statement: Commerce vertical expected FY27 EBITDA of INR 180-185 crores.
items.quote: So we have a leadership position in this space, expected to deliver between INR180 crores to INR185 crores for FY27 as an EBITDA.

items.statement: Adding 15 new B.Com colleges in FY27, doubling managed colleges; first-year investment causes minor EBITDA dip.
items.quote: We are literally doubling our managed colleges in FY27 compared to what we had as of March '26. So the first year is an investment, which obviously we are taking charge on our P&L.

items.statement: Commerce FY27 EBITDA margin to dip 4-5% due to new college investments; breakeven first year, profitable from second.
items.quote: So a minor dip that you are seeing in EBITDA is because of expansion that we are doing into managed colleges.

items.statement: Fees increase 5-10% annually, in line with or ahead of inflation.
items.quote: And typically, our fees goes up by about anywhere between 5% and 10% every year in keeping and just ahead of the inflation in the economy.

items.statement: B.Com enrollment expected to grow ~15% to 19,000+ students this year.
items.quote: So last year, we had a total enrollment of 17,000 students. Current year, based on this trend which we are having, we are expecting to be at 19,000 plus. So sharp growth of almost 15% as we're expecting.

items.statement: Operating challenges include lower CA pass rates, exam frequency changes, location and faculty hiring.
items.quote: At the same time, we remain mindful of certain operating challenges, including lower CA pass percentages, change in number of exams conducted per year, identifying suitable high potential locations for expansion and attracting quality faculty and manpower at scale.

items.statement: Demerger final approval expected by July 2026; listing by end-July or mid-August.
items.quote: We remain on track to receive final approval by July 2026. Upon completion of this process, J.K. Shah Commerce Education Limited will become a separate listed entity, enabling sharper strategic focus, efficient capital allocation and long-term shareholder value creation.

items.statement: Asset split on demerger approximately 35:65 between non-commerce and commerce entities.
items.quote: So on the appointment date, it will happen based on the assets, which are there in the company, net assets, so we expect it to be -- if you ask me approximately it will be 35:65 ratio.

items.statement: 75% of warrants outstanding, due August 2026; will be split proportionately in demerger.
items.quote: So out of the warrants, 75% are yet to be subscribed due are on August '26 it is. So based on their near future, they will subscribe to the balance warrants.

items.statement: Vocational North America entity retained, to be sold after RBI approvals.
items.quote: It will be long term. So based on the RBI approvals, everything, we'll be planning to sell it.

items.statement: Q4 government test prep loss due to INR 5 crores impairment; one-time, full year positive EBITDA.
items.quote: So in the quarter 4, the reason was because of one of the segments of the business. So there was a impairment testing being conducted as a part of audit procedures. So that effect has been taken for INR5 crores. Otherwise, there was a positive EBITDA of INR 2 crores for the year. It is a onetime activity, which we have

items.statement: Management targets 20% revenue growth in the current year while maintaining margins.
items.quote: I'm looking forward to working closely with the leadership team to drive aspirational yet achievable growth of 20% in the current year while maintaining margins.

items.statement: FY26 growth would have been 18-20% if seasonal demand were normal; business positioned for ~20% growth next year.
items.quote: Had seasonal demand been at normal levels, growth could have been closer to 18%–20%.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~INR 45 crores per year; Gurugram additional ~INR 400 crores; other projects INR 65-70 lakhs per bed.
items.quote: Maintenance capex is approximately INR 45 crores per year across our network of around 25 units.

items.statement: Total investment for Coimbatore, Pune, Indore, etc. ~INR 300-350 crores; Gurugram INR 400-500 crores over next two years.
items.quote: In addition, we expect to invest approximately INR 400–500 crores in the Gurugram projects over the next two years.

items.statement: ~900 beds in execution phase, expected to complete in ~2.5 years; excluding Gurugram ~450 beds.
items.quote: With the current expansions, what we have nearly 900-plus beds in the execution phase, which are all likely to kind of complete in about 2.5 years' time.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 31.5%; FY26 margin 32%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the current quarter stood at 31.5%, while for FY26, our EBITDA margin stood at 32%.

items.statement: ARPOB grew ~8%, driven by case mix, fertility, and pricing increases; ARPP expected to grow 5-6% annually.
items.quote: ARPOB has grown by about 8%, right? In our case, ARPOB growth is predominantly driven by case mix.

items.statement: Mature hospitals expected to reach ~60% occupancy; blended occupancy 56-57%.
items.quote: For the coming year, we believe mature hospitals should be able to operate at around 60% occupancy.

items.statement: Fertility business expected to grow ~25% YoY for at least next three years.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect the fertility business to continue growing at approximately 25% year-on-year for at least the next three years.

items.statement: International business impacted by geopolitical issues; revenue flat at ~INR 28.9 crores in FY26.
items.quote: International patient revenue remained broadly flat during FY26 at approximately INR 28.9 crores.

items.statement: No debt; cash ~INR 600 crores; all expansions funded through internal accruals, no incremental borrowing foreseen.
items.quote: We currently have no debt on our books and hold close to INR ~700 (it is ~600 Cr, regret the error) crores in cash and cash equivalents.

items.statement: Indore 100-bed hospital capex ~INR 65-70 lakhs per bed; partner builds, Rainbow invests in fit-outs.
items.quote: It is still at an early stage, but similar to our other regional spoke hospitals, the investment would likely be in the range of INR 65–70 lakhs per bed.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target over INR5,000 crores; EBITDA margin 20%+ if cell line fully operational.
items.quote: Sir, FY28 we are targeting more than INR5,000 crores of the top-line revenue. And if the full cell line should be operational then EBITDA should be 100%, 20% plus.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth at least 60%, similar to FY26.
items.quote: we definitely we assure that whatever the growth in FY 26 should be there, the revenue growth in FY27 at least should be there.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin 14-15% with aluminum integration; 20%+ from FY28.
items.quote: 14%-15% is where we are looking for. And if the conditions changes and if there is any further margin expansion then we will communicate to investors accordingly.

items.statement: FY27 total capex INR2,500 crores: INR1,500 crores cell line, INR1,000 crores KUSUM.
items.quote: So, all-in-all, INR1,500 crores of capex for cell line and INR1,000 crores of capex in KUSUM . So, all-in-all, INR2,500 crores capex this year.

items.statement: Current order book 1.6-1.8 GW; 50% of FY27 capacity already booked.
items.quote: Sir, this year order book size is nearly 1.6 gigawatt to 1.8 gigawatt, and next year with AL CM already we have done M oU with some companies and also M oUs with some companies are in pipeline

items.statement: FY26 sales mix: 85% non-DCR, 15% DCR.
items.quote: FY26 around 85% non-DCR and 15% DCR.

items.statement: Non-DCR module price INR13-14/watt; DCR INR20-22/watt.
items.quote: Price is you can say the last quarter the price non-DCR is around INR13 to INR14 per watt and DCR is from INR20 to INR22 per watt. That is Mono PERC and TOPCon.

items.statement: Raw material price increases may pressure margins; some absorbed, some passed on.
items.quote: Maybe some margin should be on pressure sid e, but we believe that on delta basis , some margin, we will absorb and some margin, we will pass on through our customers also.

items.statement: FY27 module production and sales target 2 GW; DCR extra, total 2.5-3 GW.
items.quote: For FY27 nearly from 2 gigawatt of production and 2 gigawatt of sales from the module line we are targeting.

items.statement: Wafer and ingot capex estimated INR1,000-1,200 crores, DPR under progress.
items.quote: Around sir, but DPR is under progress, but I think that some something around INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Peak debt expected INR1,500 crores in FY27; IREDA loan INR1,134 crores at 8.95-9.20%.
items.quote: It is it is close to INR1,500 crores peak debt in this year, ‘26-‘27.

items.statement: Cell plant COD targeted Q3 FY27; full ramp-up by Q1 FY28.
items.quote: our 4.5 gigawatt solar cell project at Narmadapuram is progressing as planned, with COD targeted in Q3 of FY27

items.statement: IPP KUSUM portfolio target 400 MW by FY27; revenue INR135 crores in FY27, INR300 crores in FY28.
items.quote: In the EPC and IPP segment, we continue to scale our execution capabilities with a targeted IPP portfolio of 400 megawatt by FY 27.

items.statement: Non-ALMM module overcapacity and price pressure; cell factory to mitigate in six months.
items.quote: Sir, in the market there are non-ALMM compliant modules, orders are already available to the tune of maybe 30 -gigawatt or so. And in the next six months , we would be starting our cell factory then this pressure won't be applicable on us.

items.statement: FY27 growth expected in line with FY26; H2 stronger than H1; Q1 in line with Q4.
items.quote: Overall, we do expect the growth in FY27 to be in line with what it was in FY26, supported by an improving industry cycle, execution of recent business rewards and wins and a gradual recovery across the end markets.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be comfortably above 20% in FY27, depending on volume ramp-up and delivery mix.
items.quote: We have said consistently that 20% EBITDA is sustainable over the cycle. And as volumes build through FY27, we expect to operate comfortably above that level.

items.statement: Capex plans unchanged at 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue.
items.quote: Madhur, our capex plans remain unchanged at about 2.5% to 3. 5% of our revenue, and that is consistent, and we will not be deviating from there.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month new business wins exceed INR225 crores, up 12.5% QoQ.
items.quote: our new business momentum a ctually has gained meaningful traction with trailing 12-month business wins exceeding INR22 5 crores, growing over 12.5% over quarter- on-quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 24%; FY26 full year 22%.
items.quote: Uniparts delivered a n EBITDA margin of 24% and 22% EBITDA margin for the full year FY26.

items.statement: FX pass-through netted against inflation in customer contracts.
items.quote: when we speak to our customers and we talk about FX pass-throughs, we also, at the same time, net it off against the inflation increase that happens.

items.statement: North America construction equipment demand to grow in FY27, H2 better than H1.
items.quote: In North America, customers' commentary and industry data point to continued growth in FY27 for construction equipment, with demand expected to gradually strengthen through the year and the second half being better than the first half.

items.statement: Europe construction equipment market passed cyclical low, modest growth expected.
items.quote: Specifically coming to Europe, the construction equipment m arket appears to have passed its cyclical low with early signs of recovery becoming more visible in qua rter 4 of '26.

items.statement: North America small agriculture expected ~5% growth in FY27.
items.quote: Overall, the segment is poised for approximately 5% growth in FY27, i n line with industry estimates.

items.statement: Large ag in North America still down mid-to-high teens YoY; Europe improving.
items.quote: In North America and particularly, the industry volumes for large tractors conti nues to track down in the mid- to-high teens year- on-year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: warehousing 51%, direct exports 26%, India local 14%, US local 8% in FY26.
items.value: 51% warehousing, 26% direct exports, 14% India local, 8% US local
items.quote: the warehousing channel has given us about 51% of sales. Direct exports is about 26%. India local delive ries is about 14% and U.S.A. local deliveries is about 8%.

items.statement: Fire incident at Ludhiana facility; rebuilding on track, fully insured including loss of profit.
items.quote: The incident is fully covered under our insurance policy and the claim was filed during the quarter. We expect normal operations to return on schedule.

items.statement: West Asia escalation caused supply chain uncertainty and input price inflation, partly mitigated by FX.
items.quote: In March, a fresh escalation in West Asia introduced supply chain uncertainty that required swift action. Our teams responded with agility, putting alternate arrangeme nts in place rapidly to ensure uninterrupted customer supplies.

items.statement: Targeting 15-18% growth in revenue and EBITDA for next three to four years.
items.quote: Based on current project visibility and the operational ramp-up, we are targeting 15% to 18% growth in both revenue and EBITDA for next three, four years.

items.statement: Invested ~Rs.400 Crores in FY2026; plan similar spending in FY2027.
items.quote: We have invested approximately Rs.400 Crores capital during the financial year 2026. And we plan to maintain a similar level of spending for the FY 2027.

items.statement: Dedicated block at Atali expected to generate Rs.250-300 Crores topline.
items.quote: I think depending on how we configure this, it can have potential of close to Rs.250 Crores to Rs.300 Crores topline also from a single block.

items.statement: Dedicated blocks at Atali anticipated to have capex turn of 1.5x to 2x.
items.quote: I think for the dedicated blocks, we anticipate capex turn of 1.5x to 2x.

items.statement: Line of sight of close to USD 100 million in CDMO segment.
items.quote: And that is how we have projected line of sight of close to USD 100 million in CDMO segment going forward.

items.statement: Raw material cost impact of 5% to 7% due to solvent and other cost escalation.
items.quote: I think anywhere between 5% in raw material, we are seeing this overall impact of solvents and other cost escalation 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Chinese rebate removal led to 11-13% price increase in Xanthine.
items.quote: I think Chinese rebate was close to 11% or 13% and that is what I think overall the price has increased due to that.

items.statement: API/intermediates expected to surpass FY2025 numbers in FY2027.
items.quote: We will be able to surpass the FY2025 numbers of API / Intermediates.

items.statement: Xanthine new capacity can generate well beyond Rs.1000 Crores revenue.
items.quote: And in terms of overall revenue we feel that with this current new capacity expansion, it can be well beyond Rs.1000 Crores from the Xanthine newly added capacity and already whatever that we are doing.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing logistics hurdles and rising energy costs, straining profitability.
items.quote: The impact of ongoing war, geopolitical tension in West Asia has caused significant environmental shocks, including logistics hurdles and rising energy costs.

items.statement: EBITDA catch-up from current capexes expected to take at least one year.
items.quote: I think it will take at least one year from now for the current capexes, which are coming on stream in Q1 to meaningfully contribute to the EBITDA and normalization to happen.

items.statement: Targets 175,000 MT total capacity in 12-15 months; 65k CRF, 85k NSEPL, 25k CSCL.
items.quote: we will be able to do 175,000 metric tonnes in totality with NS Engineering, in totality in terms of volume with NS Engineering, with Cosmic CRF, with Cosmic Springs and Engineers forging division and Spring division.

items.statement: Springs volume to reach 10,000-12,000 MT in FY27 and 22,000-23,000 MT in FY28.
items.quote: In FY27 this will go up to somewhere around 10,000 to 12,000 metric tonnes. By FY28 you will be achieving roughly 22,000 to 23,000 metric -- 23,000 metric tonnes in totality.

items.statement: Expects 88-89% utilization in standalone, ~48,000-50,000 MT, if order book and execution go well.
items.quote: if order books are great and everything execution goes fine, you should touch roughly 88%, 89% which is roughly 48,000 to 50,000 tonnes in totality, in standalone

items.statement: Aims to cross 90% capacity utilization next year and further increase installed capacity year after next.
items.quote: we’re doing our best to cross 90% by next year of this install capacity and further on, increase the install capacity to next to next year as well.

items.statement: Forging unit to start commercial production in next nine months.
items.quote: we are very hopeful by the next nine months we will go into complete commercial productions for the same.

items.statement: Current order book is INR760 crores, split between infrastructure and railway items.
items.quote: The total order book that we are carrying right now is INR760 crores which is divided into two parts, the infrastructure items as well as the railway items.

items.statement: Spring margins to rise to ~10% PAT after RDSO license, then 15-18% PAT.
items.quote: the moment you get the license, which I said, which we should get by next month hopefully, your percentage margins on the first part will shoot up to approximately 10% and then going up to almost 15% to 18%.

items.statement: Plans to acquire remaining 26% stake in NS Engineering to consolidate ownership.
items.quote: for NS Engineering we plan to bring the entire 26% that has been outside because Cosmic holds to 74% of the NS Engineering and 26% is held by a couple of investors and group companies.

items.statement: Awaiting CoC for Amzen; upon approval will pay and take over asset.
items.quote: we are awaiting the CoC that should happen any point in time. And moment CoC happens, by God’s grace, we will achieve the LOI where we make the payment and we’ll take over the asset.

items.statement: Plans to enter sea freight container manufacturing, adding to top and bottom lines.
items.quote: we are also planning to move into manufacturing of sea freight containers. And there’s a reason for that. The reason is you need similar amount of equipments, machinery to manufacture sea freight containers that you need to build pretty much all the items that are mentioned in the Amzen portfolio.

items.statement: Railway sector cyclical; infra and railway can be interchanged based on demand.
items.quote: we’ve seen a, the loss of tailwind in the railways over the last 1, 1.5 years. But there’s no point in crying over spilt milk because we all know it’s cyclical in nature.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations turned positive at INR3.5 crores from negative INR90 crores.
items.quote: the cash flow from operations was INR90 crores in negative which has become INR3.5 crores positive.

items.statement: FY27 volume guidance of 122,000-130,000 MT; revenue could be 20-25% higher if conditions favorable.
items.quote: Next year in FY27 you will have roughly 122,000 to 130,000 metric tonnes of capacity that you will outflow.

items.statement: FY29 target of 350,000 MT total volume, implying ~INR3,500 crores revenue at INR100,000 average pricing.
items.quote: FY 2029, you should look at total 0o£ 350,000 metric tonnes in totality. And if I'm right by my judgment, at that point in time, INR100,000 at an average pricing will give you something like INR3,500 crores

items.statement: Amzen project to cost INR400 crores, building capacity for 7,200 wagons per annum.
items.quote: Amzen is a project that will cost you INR400-o0dd crores, give and take INR10 crores here and there. Because you want to build it to 7,200 wagons an annum.

items.statement: Plan to take INR200 crores debt for Amzen; no dilution needed as project is funded.
items.quote: You'll take a loan of INR200-0dd crores. Do you need to dilute if that is something that is there in everybody’s mind? See, dilution will only come if we have something more than this. This is funded for.

items.statement: Expects 10% PAT margin on FY29 revenue of INR3,500 crores.
items.quote: You’ll be making almost 10% of the top lines that I just mentioned in FY29.

items.statement: Expects raw material prices to rise 7-10% in H2 FY27, which may lead to higher finished goods prices.
items.quote: So in the second half, not the first half but the second half the prices will shoot up to the best of my understanding. The prices will shoot up by more than 7% to 10%.

items.statement: Indian Railways needs 40,000 wagons annually for next seven years; current industry capacity only 40,000-45,000 wagons.
items.quote: You will have to have, sir, 40,000 wagons being pulled out for the next seven years.

items.statement: Amzen will be the biggest growth driver, equivalent to 90% of existing four units combined.

items.quote: We expect capex to remain in the range of 6% to 6.5% of our manufacturing revenue, reflecting ongoing investments in capacity and capability.

items.statement: New order from fastest-growing 2W/3W OEM for exhaust systems and fuel tanks; peak annual revenue INR90 crores.
items.quote: Production for these programs will be supported through a brownfield expansion at our Bangalore facility, with production slated to begin in Q2 FY '26-'27 and a peak annual revenue of INR90 crores.

items.statement: Major new order from Japanese 2W OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue ~INR220 crores.

items.statement: Raw material cost fluctuations passed through to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.
items.quote: However, our business operates on a back-to-back pricing model for raw materials. This means that any fluctuation in input costs is effectively passed through to our customers, with a certain lag.

items.statement: Plans to pass on fuel and labor costs to customers over time; transportation costs still under discussion.
items.quote: I think when it comes to passing these on to customers, we'll be looking to pass on the fuel costs and labor costs over a period of time to our customers, while on the transportation costs, we're still in discussions with a couple of our key OEMs and that is something that we'll get more clarity on going forward.

items.statement: 2W content per vehicle grew 65-70% this year; 4W/CV content grew 40-45% with H-One addition.
items.quote: In our two-wheeler segment, content per vehicle grew by 65% to 70% during this year. In our four-wheeler and commercial vehicle segments, supported by the addition of H-One, content per vehicle grew by around 40% to 45%.

items.statement: One-time operational loss of INR94.7 million in Belrise Aerospace and Defense due to startup and acquisition costs.
items.quote: Another thing I would like to note is that we had a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 million in Q4 FY26 in our subsidiary, Belrise Aerospace and Defense, due to startup costs related to overhauling of machinery, legal and professional expenses, and personnel expenses related due to our acquisition, Belrise SDM, whi

items.statement: Expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027; one-time loss not recurring.
items.quote: We expect this loss to be one-time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.

items.statement: QIP of up to INR2,000 crores is only an enabling resolution; will update on progress.
items.quote: At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution. I would also like to clarify that up to INR2,000 crores, we will come back to you on the right time if there's any further progress on this.

items.statement: Aerospace and defense targeted to contribute upwards of 10% of revenues in the medium term.
items.quote: We want it to be a meaningful contributor to our revenues, growing upwards of 10%.

items.statement: Board approved merger of two group entities into listed company at close to book value.
items.quote: Fifth, we also obtained Board approval for the merger of two group entities into the listed company at close to book value, which will help simplify the group structure and improve operational efficiencies going forward.

items.statement: Expects 25% revenue growth in FY27 with 14-15% EBITDA margins.
items.quote: Coming to FY27, we are expecting a 25% revenue growth with 14% to 15% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Welded capacity expansion adds 8,000 MTPA at ~INR40 crores, funded via internal accruals and term loans.
items.quote: The welded capacity expansion adds 8,000 metric ton per annum of our new capacity at an investment of approximately INR40 crores through internal accruals and term loans.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at ~INR100 crores.
items.quote: Almost INR100 CR addition would be there for the current FY27.

items.statement: Current order book is ~INR175 crores, executable over 3-4 months.
items.quote: It's around INR175 crores.

items.statement: Raw material prices up 25-30%, fully passed on to customers.
items.quote: Currently, the prices for base material in stainless steel has increased by 25% to 30%. But as we mentioned that these prices will be carried forward to the customer in the – what we say that, when we dispatch the orders or when we book the orders, we usually take the current prices of the raw material.

items.statement: Targeting 40% export and 60% domestic revenue mix going forward.
items.quote: For the future revenue, which is targeted as a balance of 40% export and 60% domestic mix with continued focus on international expansion.

items.statement: Welded segment opens new end-use sectors: data centers, water treatment, construction, HVAC.
items.quote: The welded segment opens new end-use sectors for us, that is data centers , water treatment, construction, and HVAC, which primarily used welded products.

items.statement: March gas disruption shut plant for 15-17 days, impacting Q4 revenue by ~INR16 crores.
items.quote: In the absence of gas supply disruption, revenue could have been approximately INR140 crores for the quarter. But the gas cut in late March was a single largest revenue headwind, curtailing production at a critical period.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned; additional capacity funded via internal accruals and term loans.
items.quote: So, for now, we don't have any plan for diluting any more equity. The additional capacity as I mentioned earlier, which we are doing is from internal accruals and term loans. Yes, so there won't be any more dilution, yes.

items.statement: Solar project to save INR8.63 crores annually, improving EBITDA margins.
items.quote: The project is expected to generate 1 37 lakh KWH annually, resulting in estimated electricity cost saving of INR8.63 crore s per year, while also improving EBITDA margins by reducing our dependence on grid power and buffering utility price fluctuations.

items.statement: Seamless utilization to reach optimum in FY28; welded in FY29.
items.quote: So, the optimum utilization for welded we will reach in FY29 and for seamless we will reach at optimum in FY28.

items.statement: FY27 utilization: seamless ~70%, welded ~25%.
items.quote: For FY27, for seamless we will be operating at almost 70% of the utilization and for welded we will be doing I think this year would be around 25% out of the installed capacity.

items.statement: Welded project delayed to H2 FY27 due to geopolitical issues and supply chain challenges.
items.quote: So, all of this, because of all of these reasons, the project is slightly delayed.

items.statement: Inventory days to reduce to 160-170 days in FY27 from 217 days.
items.quote: So, the inventory days will go down in FY27 and it will remain in the range of 160 to 170 days for the future years.

items.statement: Targets FY28 turnover of INR500+ crore with EBITDA of INR90+ crore.
items.value: 500 plus turnover with the EBITDA of 90 plus
items.quote: Yes, in fact, FY28 we are targeting for 500 plus turnover with the EBITDA of 90 plus.

items.statement: New capacity to contribute INR100-125 crore revenue in FY27.
items.quote: We are expecting between INR100 crores to INR125 crores which will be contributing in the financial year FY26 - ‘27.

items.statement: Project cost increased to INR130-135 crore from earlier INR100 crore.
items.quote: But the new project, which is having a capex of about -- in fact, now the project cost has risen from what we were anticipating earlier, it will be around INR130 to INR135 crores.

items.statement: Incremental capex of INR30-32 crore to be funded from internal resources.
items.quote: Now this incremental about INR30-INR32 crores because of the various reasons, we are going to fund it from internal resources.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 18-19%.
items.quote: We always have been maintaining that our EBITDA margin will be within 18% to 19%.

items.statement: Raw material price fluctuations passed on to customers; absolute margins remain intact.
items.quote: So, our net margin always remains intact and any fluctuation in the raw material prices are directly passed on to the customer.

items.statement: PLA price increased from INR195-197/kg pre-war to INR205/kg.
items.value: INR195, INR197 a kg; INR205 a kg
items.quote: And PLA price before the war was around INR195, INR197 a kg. Today it is around INR205 a kg.

items.statement: Existing capacity expected to reach optimal utilization in FY27.
items.quote: We are expecting that. We are targeting for that.

items.quote: No, paper cup is not seasonal. That's why I said all our new projects are food containers and they are not seasonal.

items.statement: Straw utilization capped at 35% due to seasonality; no further capex planned.
items.quote: See, I don't think it can go beyond 35%. If I average out the total yearly demand, it will never exceed 35 %.

items.quote: Today, my inventory in hand is more than 3 months.

items.quote: Normally, in the usual scenario, we import about 85%. And only 15% we buy from Indian oil.

items.quote: We are still saying that we will continue to grow 40% C AGR rate for three to five years easily without much of an issue.

items.quote: INR1,000 crore is the ladder which we are here in next 5 years and it will happen, sir.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain between 20% and 24% going forward, after considering commodity inflation.

items.quote: Okay, let me at least start with your CapEx, we don't expect a major CapEx involvement for the next couple of years at least, a major CapEx involvement, a small CapEx will always come in as and when the business will grow.

items.quote: So, the total CapEx requirement for Phase 1 at Hanbarwadi location is INR25 crores. Most of the CapEx has been done and the plant will be up and running by June.

items.statement: Closing order book of INR270 crores, 1.8 times FY26 revenue, with capacity and team in place.
items.quote: We have INR270 crores of the order book in our hand.

items.quote: So, please understand, what we see very clearly from a defence segment is approximately a INR1,000-odd crore worth of tender will be floated.

items.statement: Metal inflation will have a small impact on margins despite inflation considered in bids.

items.quote: Going forward, we expect that spares and service revenue will be incorporating 15% of the total revenue. This will help us to increase EBITDA margin in the upcoming period.

items.statement: Growth funding via internal accruals and bank funding; balance sheet unleveraged, no external equity raise needed.
items.quote: So, whatever the new working capital requirement will be funded by inter nal accruals and bank funding. If you look at our balance sheet, the balance sheet is not leveraged.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential of existing infrastructure is up to INR400 crores.
items.quote: We are still seeing up to INR400 crore kind of revenue we can generate out of existing infrastructure.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected meaningfully higher than FY26, surpassing FY25 numbers by close to 15%.
items.quote: I can only say that, We will surpass our FY 24 FY25 numbers by close to 15%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected around 11-13% for the full year.
items.quote: But for the whole year, I can predict that it would be around 11-13%.In between that ranges.

items.quote: So, year wise in '26 -'27, we are looking at a better margin than what we have done in '25 - '26.

items.quote: And 5,500, we are planning to procure in this year as per our plan, which we have given in the prospectus.

items.statement: Bamboo facility capex ~INR15 crores, expected peak revenue ~INR60 crores at full utilization.
items.quote: So, approximately the capex investment will go to about INR15 crores overall and the revenue, sales revenue will be roughly about INR60 crores.

items.statement: Bamboo revenue to start in H2 FY27 from new 3,000 cubic meter facility.
items.quote: So, we expect that in Q2 of next year, H2 of next year starting, we will be able to roll out good volumes out of that facility in terms of output.

items.quote: Customers are able to absorb up to 10% to 12% maximum on that area as on date. And as a strategic call, we are aligning with customers, this 10% to 12% will be for a longer term.

items.statement: Decent order book entering FY27; customers open to placing orders.

items.statement: FY28 revenue expected around INR 3,000 crore plus.
items.quote: So you can look at around INR3,000 crore s plus for FY28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at 14-15%.

items.quote: Actually INR5,700 crores is our current order book.

items.quote: around you can say about INR 1,000 crores would be additional order book which we may expect in coming days, apart from INR 5,700 crores.

items.quote: 60% solar, 30% power T&D, and approxima tely 10% from the water.

items.quote: we have set a very small target of INR100 crores now to start with in the data center.

items.quote: We are very positive in FY26-FY27, and we are taking lot of measures to cover up this revenue and we are positive on this.

items.statement: FY26 revenue fell due to softer freight levels and slow demand.

items.statement: Management guides FY2027 revenue growth of 21% to 23.5% year-on-year, with Q1 at lower end and improving in later quarters.

items.quote: We feel confident that we will improve on the cash flow in FY2027 in a very significant manner.

items.statement: OMC loyalty deal contributes 30 to 40 basis points to growth acceleration.
