items.statement: Targets INR4,000 crores revenue within next two years, with roadmap to double revenue in 3-5 years.
items.quote: Yes. So to give some color and guidance, yes, I mean, our target is still there for INR4,000 crores in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Expects FY27 top-line growth of 15% to 20%, conservatively.
items.quote: I mean conservatively because I always like to be that way but between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margins expected to stay at same 20-21% range despite raw material inflation.
items.quote: No, I think it will be the same.

items.statement: Expects some raw material cost inflation in Q1 FY27 from geopolitical and supply chain disruption.
items.quote: We expect obviously some inflationary pressure on raw materials costs during Q1 FY27 due to the ongoing geopolitical and supply chain disruption.

items.statement: Logistics cost impact around 2%, creeping up but not alarming.
items.quote: But now it is still around the same, about 2%.

items.statement: Major capex cycle complete; planning some capex within Teva facility for new dosage forms.
items.quote: We are planning some capex, but within the facility because it's huge. But that is to launch different dosage forms or something which is not already there in the plant.

items.statement: Plans to file over 200 products in UK market over next four years.
items.quote: Our next 4 years, we intend to file over 200 products in the U.K. market, increasing and creating a strong medium-term visibility.

items.statement: US pipeline to increase by about 50 products in FY27.
items.quote: So we've got a healthy pipeline, and we do see 2026 - '27 pipeline increasing by, like I mentioned, about 50-odd products in the U.S.

items.statement: Canada product approvals expected late this financial year; Europe revenue expected in second half.
items.quote: But Europe, we are expecting it to be earlier than expected. I mean within this year, we are expecting maybe second half for it to see some results.

items.statement: Actively evaluating two M&A targets; one in due diligence, expects 2027 M&A activity.
items.quote: So I'm more optimistic that, yes, 2027 will see some M&A transactions happening.

items.statement: Holds 5-6 months raw material inventory; no immediate margin impact unless war prolongs.
items.quote: But at any given time, at least on that raw material, we sit on a good 5 to 6 months of inventory at all given time.

items.statement: R&D spending to remain at 3% of revenue going forward.
items.quote: We'd like to keep it at that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance: gelatin capsules Rs.170cr, HPMC Rs.20cr, API Rs.70cr, Fermbox Rs.14cr; total Rs.274cr.
items.quote: Our revenue forecast for sales from Gelatin capsules is about Rs.170 crores, from HPMC capsule about Rs.20 crores, from API mainly which is domestic APl about Rs.70 crores, our forecast from firm box production, CMO contract about Rs.14 crores. So, we are talking about a consolidated level Rs.274 crores.

items.statement: FY27 margin guidance: HPMC EBITDA 18%, gelatin 13%, API gross 2-3% but EBITDA negative, Fermbox 20%.
items.quote: From HPMC we have assumed 18% as our EBITDA margin and from Gelatin around 13% which is what we expected to improve better now since there is a devaluation of rupee, the dollar, rupee and the recoveries are better.

items.statement: Additional Rs.25-30 crores needed for two clean rooms to achieve Rs.250 crore API target.
items.quote: Ican think about Rs. 25 crores to Rs. 30 crores of expenses could be required to put up these two clean rooms.

items.statement: Current order book backlog of 36 days for all capsule types.
items.quote: As on date, we have order book which is having a backlog of almost 36 days of all types of capsules.

items.statement: US Neutra demand slow, expected to improve in 3-6 months.
items.quote: So, at this point of time, demand is very slow in the US, and we anticipate that this should improve in about three to six months down the line.

items.statement: Shift focus to regulated market customers and value-added variants to improve margins.
items.quote: For FY27 the capsules business enters the year with two clear objectives are to optimize utilization across both our Bangalore and Puducherry facilities and to improve the product mix progressively towards regulated market customers and value-added variants.

items.statement: Consolidated net margin may remain very low in FY27 due to challenges.
items.quote: But | would say at the console level in the current year also, we might face challenges and probably we would end up with a very low consolidated net margin.

items.statement: Exploring fundraising options including BIRAC grant, preferential allotment, rights issue; promoters reluctant to dilute.
items.quote: We have also made an application under government RDI scheme to BIRAC, and | am hopeful that we might get some funding as being a deep tech company here in pharma AP! line. We expect to contribute equal amount from our side which should be in form of equity. We might do a kind of preferential allotment where the promot

items.statement: HPMC line revenue to commence in H2 FY27 after US customer approvals.
items.quote: Revenue from this line is expected to commence in the second half of FY27, subject to customer qualification and approval in the US market.

items.statement: Chinese steroidal API prices in India are below cost; company aims to move to semi-regulated/regulated customers for better margins.
items.quote: The prices which they sell to the Indian market, you will be surprised that they are much, much lower than what they sellin China and to large extent to the rest of the world. And Indian prices are very, very significantly lower, | would say and may not even cover their costs.

items.statement: API revenue target of Rs.250 crores achievable in 2-3 years with additional clean room investment.
items.quote: Yes, Rs. 250 crore target is still there in front of us. We probably need about two or three years.

items.statement: HPMC full capacity utilization could add 200 bps to EBITDA margin.
items.quote: So, we could expect, if our HPMC full capacity is utilized, we should do a top line volume of at least about 1.5 billion, about Rs. 45 crores from HPMC capsules. And that should give at least a200-basis point increase in EBITDA margin.

items.statement: US tariffs and anti-dumping duties severely impacted HPMC exports; business stopped after July.
items.quote: So, that was the one which completely stopped our business. So, this kind of high tariff, most of these importers were not able to sustain.

items.statement: Fermbox contract: they invest Rs.60 crores in equipment, revenue sharing model, expected to improve fermentation utilization.
items.quote: So, the agreement says that Fermbox will be investing a close to amount of Rs. 60 crores in various such equipment which will be placed on oursite, will be owned by them on their books and NBPL is also free to use those products in case they choose by giving them the whatever the charges applicable.

items.statement: Expects FY27 to be stronger than FY26 with growth, but no specific guidance until Q1.
items.quote: we expect to see improved demand visibility across both our businesses to make 2027 a stronger and a more positive year compared to 2026, which is firmly in place.

items.statement: FY27 margins expected to sustain at improved levels.
items.quote: we do expect FY '27 margins to sustain at improved levels.

items.statement: Animal Health on track to build INR500 crores+ business in next 4-5 years.
items.quote: we're still on track with the guidance that we gave you in September to build a INR500 crores plus business in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR149 crores for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, CDMO capacity.
items.quote: During the year, we have incurred capital expenditure of INR149 crores for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, and expanding CDMO capacities.

items.statement: Impairing INR47 crores of multipurpose agrochemical facility, retooling INR250 crores for pharma/animal health.
items.value: INR47 crores impairment; INR250 crores retooling
items.quote: We're impairing INR47 crores and the balance INR250 crores of retooling to build in new lines for our Pharma and Animal Health business.

items.statement: Planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY28.
items.quote: Our next milestone in this journey will be the planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY '28.

items.statement: Pharma order book intact; Q4 lost business expected to return in next few quarters.
items.quote: The Order book is still there. The order book is intact, but for the quarter 4, we have lost the business. But it will come back in the next few quarters, as Manoj said.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 20.3% over previous quarter.
items.quote: For the quarter, revenue stood at INR519 crores with EBITDA margins improving to 20.3% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 12.9%.
items.quote: For FY26, revenue stood at INR1,713 crores with EBITDA margins at 12.9%.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures from geopolitical developments; customer-supported price pass-through to partially offset.
items.quote: Despite some near-term raw material cost pressures arising from geopolitical developments, particularly the war, which has happened over the last 3 months, we expect customer-supported price pass-through mechanisms to partially offset some of these increases.

items.statement: Solvent prices elevated; pass-through negotiations ongoing with lag effect.
items.quote: So, net-net, we will end up ensuring that there's no significant impact on the bottom line, although for 1 or 2 quarters, especially quarter 1, there could be some marginal impact because by the time the pass-through happens and the negotiations end, there's a lag effect.

items.statement: US FDA warning letter at Bangalore site impacting CDMO growth; resolution expected in next few quarters.
items.quote: We are hoping towards that. I mean that's the whole idea. It's been a year now since the warning letter came about 9 months ago. So, we expect to come out of this in the next few quarters.

items.statement: FY27 guidance to be given in Q1 FY27 results; expects better revenue than FY26.
items.quote: we'll be telling at that time. That will be more clearer then.

items.statement: FY27 to have 3-4 different income streams; guidance in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: FY27, as I told in my speeches, would definitely comprise of 3 or 4 very different kinds of incomes for the company.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 1 annual lease revenue expected to exceed INR 72 crores, possibly INR 75-77 crores.
items.quote: we believe that we'll be exceeding that INR72 crores, maybe even towards INR 75 crores or INR 77 crores.

items.statement: Lease rentals from Million Minds Phase 1 to start from Q3 FY27, partial year; full year from FY28.
items.quote: The lease rentals should be star ting from Q3, I think, of this year, that is October onwards because the project is already complete.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat targeted for completion and handover by FY27 end; entire INR 450 crores sales value to be recognized.
items.quote: by FY 27 end, we should be able to complete the entire -- not only booking of that, but also handing over.

items.statement: One 91 Thaltej sale value INR 2,100 crores, cost about INR 1,500 crores; land mostly paid, construction from internal accruals.
items.value: INR 2,100 crores sale value; INR 1,500 crores cost
items.quote: One 91 Thaltej has a sale value of INR 2,100 crores and the cost of about -- so include land cost is about INR1,500.

items.statement: May take some debt in FY27 along with internal accruals to fund projects.
items.quote: So you might see some debt in the current year, coupled with our internal accruals to fund all these projects.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 2 commercial launch in Q2 FY27; residential launch in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Phase 2 is quarter 2. Phase 2 of Million Minds is quarter 2. The residential will be in quarter 3.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 2 construction to take 3 years.
items.quote: The larger construction. That will take 3 years.

items.statement: Godhavi land monetization: 46 acres sold at INR 14.1 crores per acre; 411 acres remaining.
items.quote: only approximately 46 acres have been monetized at healthy realizations averaging around INR14.1 crores per acre

items.statement: Expected free cash flow of INR 9,950 crores from planned projects, based on conservative current rates.
items.quote: all these numbers, which is coming out in terms of INR 9,950 crores are on a conservative basis.

items.statement: Took INR 150 crores LRD loan in March 2026 for construction and acquisition opportunities.
items.quote: we have taken about INR 150 crores about loan from -- on based on our leases, which were there LOIs, which were signed.

items.statement: Acquired around 7 acres of land in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We have roughly acquired around 7 acres of land during this quarter, last quarter.

items.statement: Dividend reduced to 15% to conserve cash for growth opportunities.
items.quote: the Board discussed and then came at the 15% because good opportunities are coming up where the cash can be utilized for the growth.

items.statement: Targets 60 million tons production for FY27, including NSL.
items.quote: And in that journey, I think this year we will be targeting 60 million tons, which we hope to achieve.

items.statement: Aims to reach 100 million tons production by end of decade.
items.quote: I believe that this sets the foundation for us to achieve 100 million tons by the end of this decade.

items.statement: Expects next 2-3 years annual capex of INR7,000-10,000 crores.
items.quote: And going forward next 2, 3 years it will be in the range of INR7,000 crores to INR10,000 crores every year for the next 2, 3 years because you see most of the works are under execution and a couple of major works are just under award.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 42-43% for FY27.
items.quote: So, this will be a range-bound movement around this time also and we expect to have to maintain our EBITDA at around 42 to 43% this year. This is our expectation.

items.statement: Iron ore prices expected to remain range-bound with no sharp increase.
items.quote: I don't expect a sharp increase, they would be rather range-bound.

items.statement: Demand not a problem even for 100 million tons due to low phosphorus ore.
items.quote: So, I don't think demand is an issue at all, even for a 100 million ton production.

items.statement: RINL receivables recovery timeline uncertain but no credit risk seen.
items.quote: RINL of course we'll have to have another look what their plans are. We are in touch with RINL. Hopefully once it turns around, it is a, as you know, it's a 100% government-owned company. So we don't see any risk.

items.statement: Deposit 4 guidance: 1 million ton this year, 2 million next, ramping to 7 million peak.
items.quote: And this year, I think the guidance would be around 1 million ton out of Deposit 4. So and next year it will be 2 million ton, followed by once the infrastructure is all ready by another one and a half to two years, then it will be ramped up to 7 million ton, which is the peak rated capacity of Deposit 4.

items.statement: Coal production guidance: 0.75-1 million ton this year from Tokisud.
items.quote: And our guidance for Q2 would be around 0.75 million ton to 1 million ton of coal this year.

items.statement: No immediate plans to leverage balance sheet; capex to be funded internally.
items.quote: As of now there are no immediate plans of leveraging our balance sheet. The current visibility is that we should be able to service all our capex and acquisition requirements through internal resources.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining Q4 performance; intends operating margin better than FY26's 13.8%, maybe 1% plus.
items.quote: But we intend to do better than last year overall operating margin, which is 13.8%. So it should be better, maybe 1% plus.

items.statement: Wants to grow volumes at least 4% to 5% over next two years, with caution.
items.quote: But overall, we want to grow at least 4% to 5% in volume with product.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR180-200 crores next year versus INR130 crores last year.
items.quote: Last year, we incurred around INR130 crores. Next year, we have planned around INR180 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Took calibrated price hikes of 15-18% at consumer level across categories to offset input and wage inflation.
items.quote: So roughly around 15% to 18% is the increase . In some categories, it is lesser and some categories, it is more.

items.statement: Overall cost increase around 15-20% on cost side as on date, including material and labor.
items.quote: So we can say around 15% to 20% increase will be there overall on the cost side as on date.

items.statement: Price increases will remain; no rollback expected as raw material unlikely to settle soon.
items.quote: No. I don't think there is any possibility that raw material will settle down soon. So this price increase will remain.

items.statement: Intends to improve gross and operating margins, but must stay competitive on passing costs to consumers.
items.quote: The gross margin intent is to improve, and overall operating margin should also improve. That's what we are trying.

items.statement: Widening premium playbook with sneakers and lifestyle products; Sparx extending to INR2,500-2,800 MRP.
items.quote: Now we are thinking about how we can offer more products at INR2,500 also. So the price and the premium we are increasing.

items.statement: Current mix: men 70%, women 25%, kids 5%; focus to improve women and kids contribution.
items.quote: So, for us, men's contribution is 70%, 25% is women and 5% is kids. So more of our focus will be on women and kids to improve.

items.statement: Plans to open 100 new EBO stores; 30-40% in first half, most by December; each store INR30-35 lakhs.
items.quote: In first half, we will be able to open at least 30%, 40% of the 100. So, by December, most of them should be ready.

items.statement: April and May were better; too early to say on June; monitoring consumer reaction post price hikes.
items.quote: It's too early to say, but April and May were better. May is still going on. And let us see how June goes.

items.statement: Cautious on near-term due to geopolitical uncertainty, inflationary pressure possibly affecting consumer sentiment.
items.quote: While the company has recently taken some calibrated price increases to offset input cost inflation, a full impact on demand and consumption pattern is still evolving and requires close monitoring.

items.statement: Ad spend at 4-5% of net sales, to be maintained in FY27 with shift toward digital.
items.quote: And we'll continue to see the same kind of ratio of 4% to 5% of net sales for '27?

items.statement: Brand mix: Sparx ~40%, Hawaii ~25%, Flite ~35% of revenue.
items.quote: So our contribution from Sparx is around 40%; Hawaii is around 25% and Flite is 35%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at 14-15%, lower than earlier 15-20% due to geopolitics.
items.quote: we still hope that we can be at the lower or 14%, 15% growth we still hope that we will get.

items.statement: Defense revenue FY27 expected INR250-300 crores, 75-80% capacity utilization.
items.quote: We have already some questionnaires some people had asked , and they are expecting almost INR250 crores to INR300 crores. So, I agree to that view.

items.statement: Defense EBITDA margin to normalize to 30-35% in coming years, not sustain 68-70%.
items.quote: In the coming years, what the guidance we have given of 30%, 35%, it will prevail.

items.statement: Defense capacity expansion to 4 lakh shells with INR400 crores outlay, timing uncertain FY27/FY28.
items.quote: in our Goodluck Defence and Aerospace, we have a plan to augment our capacity, which has a capital outlay of INR400 crores, but it will be sprawled maybe in this financial year or it may be carried forward to the next financial year also.

items.statement: Adding 40,000-45,000 tons capacity in GI conduit pipes and front fork tubes in FY27.
items.quote: in the coming financial year, we will be doing almost 40,000 to 45,000 ton capacity addition.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube capacity utilization to rise to 65-70% in FY27 from 50%.
items.quote: in this year, we hope th at we will be able to d o it to 65% to 70%, number one.

items.statement: GI conduit pipes EBITDA margin 15-20% sustainable; front fork tubes 15-16%.
items.quote: for the calculation purpose, you take it from 15% to 20% margin, which will be sustainable in future.

items.statement: Input cost increases being passed to customers with 3-6 month lag.
items.quote: we are trying to pass it on to the customers, but it is always with a time lag. So, it may take 3 months, to 1 quarter to 2 quarters to pass all these increases.

items.statement: Steel business volume growth expected 13-15% in FY27.
items.quote: in FY27, we hope that this West Asia crisis is solved and our volume growth, it will be 13% to 15% band in this coming financial year for the steel business, what you are asking, particularly.

items.statement: Exports may be impacted 5-10% due to longer transit times from West Asia crisis.
items.quote: As far as the exports are concerned, exports because of time duration taken in reaching the consignment, it is taking more ti me. So, it may impact some 5%, 10%

items.statement: Artillery shell demand 8-9 million vs supply 2-3 million; supply constrained for 4-5 years.
items.quote: the demand today is 8 million to 9 million shells, whereas the quantity available or quantity to be started in the next 1 or 2 years, it may be 2 million to 3 million.

items.statement: No comment on defense IPO; details to be shared at appropriate time.
items.quote: Basically, on this issue, I will prefer no comments, because it is on the wheels, and we will le t you know when the right time comes.

items.statement: Net debt INR1,000 crores (working capital INR800 crores, term loan INR200 crores); cash INR50 crores.
items.quote: Net debt position, working capital loans is INR800 crores and term loan is INR200 crores. Total INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement is sustainable, no transitory elements.
items.quote: There is no worry. Gross margin will be sustained. It is a sustainable margin, what we have given.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance: EXIM 8%, domestic 15%, overall 9.5%.
items.quote: EXIM, I would like to give a guidance of 8%. Domestic, I would like to give guidance of 15%. Overall, will be 9.5%.

items.statement: Board approved FY27 capex budget of INR945 crores, may increase at midyear review.
items.quote: in this financial year, yesterday, Board of Directors have approved a capex budget of INR945 crores. We may be increasing the budget during the midyear review

items.statement: Will maintain EBITDA margin between 24% and 25% in coming years.
items.quote: in the coming years also, we will maintain EBITDA between 24% to 25%. We are quite clear on that.

items.statement: Will offer competitive tariff for double-stack upper deck, sharing haulage savings with customers.
items.quote: we will be coming out with a very competitive tariff that will be light cargo, which is at present moving by road.

items.statement: Expects JNPT rail coefficient to rise to 18-19% in FY27 and 30-35% in 3 years.
items.quote: in this FY, I'm sure from 15%, at least, it will go to 18% to 19%.

items.statement: Targets at least 1 million tons of bulk cement in tank containers in domestic this fiscal.
items.quote: I'm quite positive that in this financial year itself, we will be able to do at least 1 million tons of bulk cement in tank containers in domestic.

items.statement: Board approved procurement of 2,000 more tank containers, adding to 1,000 earlier approved.
items.quote: Board of Directors further approved the procurement of 2,000 more tank containers, apart from 1,000 tank containers approved earlier.

items.statement: Gunny bales and Morbi tiles volumes currently below normal but expected to revive quickly.
items.quote: Right now, they are below that, but there are indications that very quickly, they will be increasing.

items.statement: No long-term guidance due to geopolitical uncertainties; will review midyear.
items.quote: In the present market scenario, I feel it is better not to make any long-term guidance forecast. So I will adhere to only this financial year guidance.

items.statement: DFC connectivity to JNPT to be commissioned by 1 June 2026, enabling double-stack trains.
items.quote: DFC connected to -- connectivity to JNPT will be commissioned by 1st June 2026, so we are quite ready.

items.statement: Signed MOU with PSA for dedicated services between JNPA and CONCOR ICDs.
items.quote: we have signed MOU with PSA that is Port of Singapore Authority for dedicated services between JNPA and CONCOR ICDs.

items.statement: CONCOR holds 30% stake in Bharat Container Shipping Line.
items.quote: CONCOR signed MOU for Bharat Container Shipping Line, in which we have a 30% stake.

items.statement: Reduced empty running of rakes by 10.5% overall, improving bottom line.
items.quote: we reduced the empty running of rakes also and by -- in EXIM by 27% and in domestic around 4%, overall, 10.5% reduction in empty running of rakes.

items.statement: Other expenses to be recurring at INR70-80 crores per quarter.
items.quote: on an average, you can see the expenses would be around INR70 crores to INR80 crores per quarter.

items.statement: No further closure or exceptional losses expected from discontinued operations or business exits.
items.quote: The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes, which are announced by the Government of India.

items.statement: OTTplay subscriptions stopped from April 1; residual servicing may cause marginal FY27 losses.
items.quote: If the unit economics of that is not working out, there might be marginal losses, etc., which will basically come into the P&L for FY 2027, but that will be a very small number.

items.statement: Shutting OTTplay contracts will have some cash impact but marginal P&L effect.
items.quote: So those will basically tantamount to cash flow. So, there will be some cash impact to shut down these contracts. But from a P&L perspective, there will be a very marginal impact of some residual subscribers, who purchased their subscriptions in March and might go up until September, but that will be a very small numbe

items.statement: No plans to return cash to shareholders; Board prefers investing in core and digital businesses.
items.quote: Well, there is none so far.

items.statement: AFE assets will be sold at earliest opportunity to maximize value; not long-term holds.
items.quote: The simple answer is yes. We are not holding these assets for the very long term. Of course, it doesn't mean that we will flip the assets within months. But at the earliest opportunity, when we think we can maximize the value for the organization, we will sell these assets.

items.statement: Other income fell INR 50 crore due to mark-to-market losses on treasury; expected to recover.
items.quote: That is what is impacting other income to the extent of INR 50 crore in the full year. Of course, there are various other small reasons, but that's the chunk of the reason which is happening there.

items.statement: Assetvault investment is non-cash AFE; no cash invested, brand AasaanWill.
items.quote: On Assetvault, you are right, the revenue is pretty small at this point in time. But as explained earlier, it's again an AFE investment. It's not a cash investment, it is our AFE investment, and there are certain marketing plans that, that company has for the market of India, where we would like to give our marketing p

items.statement: Radio: surrendered six loss-making frequencies; all remaining frequencies profitable.
items.quote: On Radio, we did an entire portfolio review where all the five loss-making frequencies now and one loss-making frequency earlier totalling to six loss-making frequencies - those are the frequencies that we've surrendered back to the Government of India. All existing frequencies are profitable frequencies and obviously

items.statement: Radio sector under pressure; will keep reviewing closely.
items.quote: Now, however, as I explained in the webinar, Radio as a sector is under a lot of pressure, but we will keep on reviewing this on a very close basis.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided.
items.quote: As per usual practice, we do not provide specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Circulation revenue up 4% overall; realization per copy marginally up; copy share increased.
items.quote: Well, overall circulation revenue is plus 4% between English and Hindi. I would say realization per copy is slightly flat here and there, but there's not a huge amount of variance in circulation revenue.

items.statement: Expects a better year ahead than FY26, barring unforeseen geopolitical events; June quarter momentum strong.
items.quote: So barring unforeseen new geopolitical events that can create supply challenges, demand challenges, we expect a better year going ahead.

items.statement: Second phase of aluminum formwork and extrusion expansion planned for end of FY27 or early FY28, capex about INR150 crores.
items.quote: We will do the second phase of expansion of our aluminum formwork and extrusion capacity towards the end of this financial year or early next financial year.

items.statement: Minor debottlenecking to raise scaffolding capacity by 10-15% this year; no significant incremental capex in FY27.
items.quote: we have already done some minor debottlenecking capex as a result of which our capacities have gone up by about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Formwork order book exceeds 4.5 lakh square meters, more than 6 months of current production capacity.
items.quote: Even today, we are sitting on order books in excess of 4.5 lakh square meters, which is more than 6 months actually of our current production capacity.

items.statement: June quarter margins expected to continue at similar levels as March quarter, excluding one-time steel discount.
items.quote: So yes, the immediate quarter under purview, the June quarter, we are seeing this continue. So we are quite confident that this quarter is going along the similar lines.

items.statement: Steel prices rose ~25% in 3 months but fully passed on; aluminum cost volatility managed via backward integration.
items.quote: Steel prices have increased by almost 25% over the last 3 months, but we've been able to pass them on. So there is no real pressure on margins.

items.statement: US tariffs fully passed on to customers; no absorption needed as tariffs apply to all countries, China pays extra 25%.
items.quote: So we don't need to absorb anything. We are able to pass this on to the customers and they are paying.

items.statement: US scaffolding demand resurgence since December 2025 is sustained; June quarter expected strong despite summer seasonality.
items.quote: At the moment, we are seeing a sustained demand resurgence. Like I said, since December '25, there has been an uptick, and it's not slowed down, and it doesn't seem to show an indication of slowing down.

items.statement: Drum closure demand stable; single-digit revenue growth expected, China growing strongly, other countries 4-5% growth.
items.quote: There has been some you know so we are on track with single-digit revenue growth. China continues to grow strongly. And the rest of the countries, we are growing at about 4%, 5% in terms of quantity and price growth.

items.statement: Engineering services revenue growing 8-10% per quarter; AI pivot creating new digital transformation opportunities.
items.quote: But the way it is growing, it is growing at about 8% to 10% every quarter. And I think that growth will continue.

items.statement: Mach One volumes soft due to real estate project execution delays; capacity utilization at 60-70%.
items.quote: As far Mach One is concerned, our capacity utilization is quite low. We are operating at about 60% to 70% capacity utilization, mainly because of slow site mobilization.

items.statement: INR20 crores one-time steel quantity discount benefit in Q4 FY26 scaffolding; forex gain INR20 crores for quarter, INR46 crores full year.
items.quote: There were some one -time benefits pertaining to quantity discounts that we obtained in this quarter for steel . This amounted to almost INR20 crores, which does not represent only the quarter.

items.statement: Yarn EBITDA at ~10%; Q1 FY27 expected to improve on better yarn spreads. Fabric division restructuring under evaluation.
items.quote: EBITDA, we are doing about 10% on EBITDA level. And I think it will in the quarter 1 of this financial year, it will improve by on account of the yarn spread being better.

items.statement: Defense division still in sampling and DRDO approval stage; no figures to share with investors currently.
items.quote: But there is nothing that we can share with the investors as of now. These are all efforts going in that direction. Defense is still there as a division, but not something which we can tell now.

items.statement: Both top line and bottom line will be positive; results visible from Q1; decent growth expected in FY27.
items.quote: I can say that both top line and bottom line will be positive. The results will be visible from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Capex requirement going forward largely nominal, INR25-30 crores maintenance capex after FY27 projects.
items.quote: Therefore, our capex requirement going forward remains largely nominal or in the range of INR25- INR30 crores, which we call as a maintenance capex once we complete our projects in the year FY27.

items.statement: Expects small increase in gross and EBITDA margins in FY27, but difficult to quantify.
items.quote: It is difficult to comment at this moment that we'll be able to increase it by how much percentage. But yes, there will be a small increase.

items.statement: Took two price increases in April; first well received, second faced issues, may take another in June.
items.quote: Yes, we have taken two price increases in the month of April, and they were quite successful.

items.statement: Crop activity expected to improve in June as monsoons hit; May sluggish due to heat.
items.quote: The crop activity, though, is expected to improve in the month of June as the monsoons hit the Indian coastline.

items.statement: Premium segment currently 60-63% of B2C; vision to reach 60-70% in next 4 years.
items.quote: At this moment, they are contributing roughly about 60% to 63%. So it's my vision to take it to 60%- 70% in next 4 years.

items.statement: Exports to grow from ~5% to 10% of revenue in next 2-3 years, driven by CDMO.
items.quote: I see it growing up to 10% in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Kaeros expected to double sales in FY27; contribute 5-8% to IIL volume.
items.quote: So, we should be at least doubling these total sales of Kaeros in this fiscal.

items.statement: Prolonged geopolitical tensions may keep raw material prices elevated and impact business.
items.quote: We'll remain mindful that prolonged geopolitical tensions may continue to impact business conditions and keep raw material price elevated for some time.

items.statement: El Nino impact and crop mix change, particularly in dry crops, are risks.
items.quote: We'll also take care of the evolving global supply chain conditions, the El Nino impact, crop mix change, particularly in the dry crops.

items.statement: Target to reduce interest cost by at least 25-30% in FY27.
items.quote: But internally, there is a target that we'll reduce it by at least 25%, 30%.

items.statement: ICS plot program to double to over INR60 crores, expanding to maize and cotton.
items.quote: So last year, we made about more than INR30-odd crores. And this year, we are going to double this number.

items.statement: Copper and fertilizer project to be operational from FY28, with revenue of around Rs 40,000 crore plus in that year.
items.quote: So, it would be downstream products, then the refinery would be operational, secondary product line operation. All will be operational in 2027-28 and we continue to have, based on the pricing, somewhere around 40,000 crores plus revenue in this year as well.

items.statement: Capex plan: Rs 4,500-5,000 crore by March 2027, another Rs 5,000 crore next year, and Rs 2,000-3,000 crore by March 2029.
items.quote: And the capital investment this year, by end of March 2027, will be at least close to Rs.4,500 to Rs.5,000 crores. Again, in the next year, as per the current plan, will be almost equivalent, another Rs.5,000 crores. And then we have another Rs.2,000 to Rs.3,000 crores by March 2029.

items.statement: Standalone dyes business targets 10-15% EBITDA margin, aiming for 12% this year.
items.quote: I think we would target somewhere between 10% to 15%. So, if we are at 12% during this year, we will be happy.

items.statement: Standalone revenue expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore in FY27, with 20% growth.
items.quote: So, the target is to cross Rs.1000 crore. So, we are expecting (+20%) growth this year. So, hopefully, we will cross Rs.1000 crore in this financial year. On a standalone basis.

items.statement: Government incentives: expected Rs 3,000-3,500 crore over 10 years, 30-35% of eligible capex.
items.quote: But we would receive roughly 30, somewhere between 30 to 35% of eligible CAPEX over a period of 10 years, right? And in absolute number, would be in the range of Rs.3,000 crores to Rs.3,500 crores to be received yearly within a period of 10 years from the date of commercial and operation beginning for both the plants.

items.statement: Dyes intermediates outlook improving due to China supply tightening from environmental measures, supporting realizations.
items.quote: The outlook for Dyes Intermediates is becoming more constructive. China's supply of key intermediates has tightened due to environmental compliance measures and production containments, which is expected to support industry dynamics and improve realizations for Indian producers going forward.

items.statement: Fertilizer trading to start from next quarter; copper trading not yet commenced.
items.quote: And the company would start trading fertilizers during this year, this financial year. So, fertilizer distribution would start probably from next quarter onwards within this year as well for the trading part of the company.

items.statement: No dividend declared for this year; board decided to retain cash for growth.
items.quote: But this year, the dividend has not been declared and is not going to be declared. I would be certain and clear for that.

items.statement: Civil construction for copper and fertilizer project 25-30% complete.
items.quote: The civil construction for the entire site, including all the units, would be till now close to 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Standalone FY27 revenue expected to increase 10% to 12%.
items.quote: Looking ahead, on a standalone basis, we expect FY27 revenue to increase by 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Opening order book about INR7,000 crores after excluding two cancelled orders worth about INR550 crores.
items.quote: The opening order book for the year is about INR7,000 crores, after excluding 2 orders worth about INR550 crores that were cancelled during the year.

items.statement: Booked new orders totaling INR1,400 crores in first two months of current quarter.
items.quote: In the first 2 months of the current quarter, we have booked new orders totaling INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBIT margin expected to be maintained at 12% to 13%.
items.quote: So in the manufacturing business, today, we are confident on 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Projects business margin expected to improve to closer to 5.5% for FY27.
items.quote: But we still think that we will actually be improving over that 4.5%. We should be closer to 5.5% for FY27.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR25 crores investment to expand Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant capacity.
items.quote: In addition, the Board at it's meeting the day before yesterday approved a further investment of INR25 crores to expand capacity at our Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant.

items.statement: Input costs rising for steel forgings, castings, chemicals, imported materials; gas shortages raised fuel costs.
items.quote: However, we are seeing increases in several input costs, including steel forgings, castings, chemicals and certain imported materials. Gas shortages have raised fuel costs; however, there has been no disruption to manufacturing operations.

items.statement: Most increased costs expected to be absorbed through normal contingency provisions.
items.quote: As of now, most of the increased costs are expected to be absorbed through normal contingency provisions.

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook remains strong in domestic and export markets.
items.quote: Looking ahead, the inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook remains strong in both domestic and export markets.

items.statement: Export revenue more than doubled to INR1,169 crores, about 22% of total revenue; expected to continue.
items.quote: Export revenue during FY26 has increased to INR1,169 crores, which is about 22% of the total revenue, up from INR532 crores in the previous year. Export revenue more than doubled year-on-year, and we expect this increased level of exports to continue.

items.statement: Export order book about INR1,450 crores as on 31st March 2026; export order book expected to rise.
items.quote: I mean our export order book is also about INR1,450 crores as on 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Isgec Hitachi Zosen FY27 revenue expected closer to INR700 crores, profit INR100 crores plus.
items.quote: We are expected to do slightly better than this. So we are hoping that revenue could be closer to INR700 crores. And the profit should be in the range of INR100 crores plus.

items.statement: Philippines business no longer classified as held for sale; sale timing uncertain, may take 1-2 years.
items.quote: While we do expect that it can happen within the next 1 or 2 years that you mentioned, but the accounting requires us to run it as a continuing operation.

items.statement: FY27 output expected at 400,000 tons, rising to 475,000-500,000 tons in FY28.
items.quote: our output is going to go from about 265,000 tons, which is where we are in FY '26 to broadly 400,000 tons in FY '27 and 500,000 tons or so, 475,000 to 500,000 tons in FY '28.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR450 crores; FY28 major portion of INR700 crores for mines.
items.quote: In FY '27, what we said is that the balance amount of Kalinganagar and Ethanol projects and the underground mines in Sukinda that we are investing. Total amount of INR450 crores planned towards capex.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins and prices higher than Q4 FY26.
items.quote: In the ongoing Q1 FY '27, we are seeing margins and price s and therefore, margins higher than what we saw in Q4.

items.statement: Domestic ferrochrome prices at INR118,000-120,000/ton; export realizations above INR120,000/ton.
items.quote: currently, I would say domestic prices are in the INR118,000 to INR120,000 a ton mark, which is a little bit higher than what we have seen in Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales expected ~80,000 tons vs normal 65,000-67,000 tons.
items.quote: As against sales of about 65,000, 67,000 tons a quarter that is normal for us. In Q1, we will be looking at about 80,000 tons because of the additional output from KNR 2, which is coming in.

items.statement: Shift from 90:10 export:domestic to 60:40 by next year.
items.quote: We are looking at going from 90-10 to 60-40 by sometime next year.

items.statement: EBITDA cost reduction of INR3,000-4,000/ton expected from KNR complex synergies.
items.quote: when entire KNR complex comprising 1 and 2 is up and running is where we are looking at a weighted average reduction in EBITDA cost by INR3,000 to INR4,000 on account of better logistics.

items.statement: KNR1 furnaces to be switched on around July 10-15 and end August/early September.
items.quote: one furnace we're looking to switch on by about 10th to 15th Jul y and the next furnace around end August, early September

items.statement: KNR2 partially built 33 MVA furnace targeting commissioning around June 2027.
items.quote: we would hope to target commissioning around June 2027.

items.statement: Coal linkage benefits of INR400-500/ton cheaper from Q3 FY27.
items.quote: those benefits will start flowing probably from Q3 of this year that coal sourcing through linkages is also the pricing is going to be about INR400 to INR500 a ton cheaper.

items.statement: South African power tariff may be net neutral for chrome units; risk if Chinese output doesn't fall.
items.quote: if ferrochrome production in South Africa picks up and Chinese ferrochrome production doesn't go down, then you will certainly see pressure on prices.

items.statement: Mining target 10 lakh tons in FY27, eventually 12 lakh tons from underground.
items.quote: FY '26, we crossed 8 lakh tons. And FY '27, the target is for 10 lakh tons.

items.statement: Renewable energy to be 35-40% of total energy consumption in FY28.
items.quote: next fiscal, FY '28, we broadly would expect about 35% to 40% of our total energy consumption to be from renewable sources.

items.statement: Hedging policy: 25-30% of net forex exposure hedged for 12-18 months.
items.quote: we look to hedge about 25% to 30% of our outstandings at any of our net foreign exchange exposure

items.statement: No further closure or exceptional losses expected from discontinued operations or business exits.
items.quote: The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes, which are announced by the Government of India.

items.statement: Marginal residual OTTplay losses expected in FY2027 from servicing existing subscriptions.
items.quote: If the unit economics of that is not working out, there might be marginal losses, etc., which will basically come into the P&L for FY 2027, but that will be a very small number.

items.statement: Advertising yields expected to be sustained at current levels or above, though competition may react.
items.quote: Well, to an extent, yes, but I won't do a carte blanche on that because there's an immediate reaction, which always comes from the competition. But our hope & prayer and even the plan that we have set out for ourselves – though we don't give forward guidance – is to keep our deals at a certain level and above not below

items.statement: Radio segment margins under pressure; all remaining frequencies are profitable after surrendering loss-making ones.
items.quote: Now, however, as I explained in the webinar, Radio as a sector is under a lot of pressure, but we will keep on reviewing this on a very close basis. But right now, all the frequencies or all the stations which were not turning in a profit, we've already surrendered those frequencies.

items.statement: Advertising revenue growth driven primarily by yield improvement, not volume.
items.quote: So, the simple answer is, the lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volume s have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry. So , it's basically pricing.

items.statement: Circulation realization per copy increased marginally; copy share increased in some markets.
items.quote: It has , but marginally because the constraint there will be competition. But you are right our realization per copy has increased.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 10% in Q4 and 8% for full year, led by yield improvement.
items.quote: A bit into the numbers for the quarter, advertising revenue growth of 10% at INR 313 crore, circulation revenue growth of 4% at INR 51 crore, operating revenue at INR 427 crore and operating EBITDA coming at INR 97 crore with a 23% margin.

items.statement: Radio revenue declined due to high base from prior year's event-led revenue and industry-wide issues.
items.quote: The segment revenue declined on account of high events-led revenue which is there sitting in the base. Business continues to be under pressure with subdued margins.

items.statement: OTTplay business discontinued due to challenging space and failure to achieve viable unit economics.
items.quote: However, in spite of our best effort, the space became increasingly challenging, especially since all the big telcos also have a significant presence. Though I must also caveat that we had already segmented our markets not as Tier 1, but Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, thereby, w e were using a different distribution channel

items.statement: Rising newsprint costs, weak rupee, supply chain disruptions, and geopolitical volatility are near-term concerns.
items.quote: In the near term though, rising newsprint costs, amplified by a weakeni ng rupee and the prevailing global environment of supply chain disruptions, trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, remains a concern that we are managing with cost discipline.

items.statement: No plans to return cash to shareholders; Board prefers investing in businesses for long-term value.
items.quote: Well, there is none so far.

items.statement: AFE assets will be monetized at earliest opportunity to maximize value; not desperate sellers.
items.quote: The simple answer is yes. We are not holding these assets for the very long term. Of course, it doesn't mean that we will flip the assets within months. But at the earliest opportunity, when we think we can maximize the value for the organization, we will sell these assets.

items.statement: Other income dropped by INR 50 crore due to mark-to-market losses on treasury investments.
items.quote: That is what is impacting other income to the extent of INR 50 crore in the full year. Of course, there are various other small reasons, but that's the chunk of the reason which is happening there.

items.statement: Projects FY27 revenue growth of 10% to 12%, largely volume-led.
items.quote: We project revenue growth of 10% to 12% in financial year '27, largely led by volumes and expect our EBITDA margin to be in the range of 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Plans INR60 crores capex over two years for manufacturing-cum-warehousing at West Bengal Hosiery Park, Kolkata.
items.quote: During FY27, the company will strengthen its in-house capacity by developing manufacturing cum warehousing facilities. And there will be a total outlay of INR60 crores, which will be spent in 2 years' time.

items.statement: Took a 4% to 5% price hike in April; may take another 2% to 3% in June-July.
items.quote: We have taken a price hike of around 4% to 5% in April and we might take another price hike maybe 2%, 3% in June, July, depending on the market condition.

items.statement: FY27 advertisement spend guidance of 6% to 7% of revenue.
items.quote: The advertisement spend for the quarter is around 4%. And the next year guidance would be the advertisement expenses would be in the range of 6% to 7% for FY27.

items.statement: Athleisure grew 20% by volume and 25% by value in Q4, driving gross margin improvement.
items.quote: The main reason is that the athleisure contributes well in this quarter 4, there is a volume growth of 20% in quarter 4 and value growth is 25% for Athleisure.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current gross margin with initial price hike and market acceptability.
items.quote: Yes, with this initial price hike and acceptability in the market, we hope that we will sustain this gross margin.

items.statement: FY27 growth split expected roughly 4-5% each from volume and value.
items.quote: Volume maybe 4%, 5%. Largely it will be a mix of both 4%, 5% each,

items.statement: Faces challenges from higher crude/raw material prices, shipping disruption raising logistics costs, and forex volatility.
items.quote: There is no potential impact on the business, but business is facing some challenges, such as increase in price of crude would lead to the rise in the prices of raw material.

items.statement: Trade discount intensity remains around 12% and will be maintained at same level.
items.quote: We will maintain the same level of discount.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% growth over next couple of years with profitability improving 50 bps annually.
items.quote: So, we target a growth of 10% to 12% for the next couple of years. And with that, every year maybe profitability, should help us increase the profitability by 50 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend of INR3 per equity share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: In line with this commitment, the Board has proposed subject to shareholders' approval a dividend of INR3 per equity share for financial year '26.

items.statement: Inventory split: raw material 13%, finished goods 54%, work in progress 33%.
items.quote: The split of inventory, the raw material is around 13%. The finished goods is around 54% and work in progress is around 33%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13% for full year, with Q1 expected to be strong.
items.quote: We are projecting for next year 13% EBITDA.

items.statement: Volume growth to outperform market by 2%; if market grows 6-7%, company grows 9%.
items.quote: So, if the market is growing by 6%-7%, we will be growing at 9%.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at around INR 150 crores, including maintenance capex of INR 40-50 crores.
items.quote: the capex for FY'27 is around INR 150 crores or so.

items.statement: Strong order book for next 18 months; secured 30,000+ tonne coke oven order for 2 batteries.
items.quote: we have a strong order book for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Seeking 1-3% price increases depending on category/segment, effective from May onwards.
items.quote: we are asking for 1% - 3% of price increases depending on the categories or the segments that we are operating.

items.statement: Margins expected to be significantly better than Q4 FY26 due to price increases and fixed cost absorption.
items.quote: our margins will be significantly better than what we have achieved in the last quarter, which is Q4 with the price increases and with the iron making fixed cost absorption that we were mentioning.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be a strong quarter with 1,000+ volumes, helped by cement season.
items.quote: But Q1, we should be back with 1,000+ volumes again.

items.statement: Cement share of revenue dropped from 13% in FY25 to 11% in FY26 due to overcapacity and competition.
items.quote: Our cement as a percentage of revenue from FY '25 to '26 also dropped because of this over competition. So, in FY '25, we had about 13%. Now it's at about 11%

items.statement: Goodwill impairment on Dalmia assets due to weaker exports, FX volatility, new competition capacity, and inflation.
items.quote: we prudently went for the impairment of the goodwill on the Dalmia assets only.

items.statement: Restructuring is fully complete; no further restructuring required.
items.quote: It is complete. No further restructuring is required, and we say this with utmost confidence.

items.statement: Dalmia assets grew 14% in FY26 with revenue INR 1,153 crores and EBITDA margin 10.8%.
items.quote: we grew in Dalmia asset by 14%. Revenue was INR 1,153 crores as against INR 1,013 crores of FY '25, so it is a 14% growth in that particular segment and revenue has gone up to 10.8% against 11.5%.

items.statement: Company ended FY26 in net cash position with net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.1x.
items.quote: ended the year in a net cash position, with net debt-to-EBITDA entering to net cash positive at 0.1x.

items.statement: FY26 cash flow from operations increased 9% year-on-year to INR 409 crores.
items.quote: Cash flow from operations increased 9% year-on-year to INR 409 crores, supported by disciplined working capital management and improved cash conversion across the business.

items.statement: FY26 revenue surpassed INR 4,000 crores for the first time, with shipments up 5% to 523 kilotons.
items.quote: Revenue from operations increased 9% year-on-year to INR 4,000 crores, while shipments grew 5% to 523 kilotons.

items.statement: FY27 volumes expected to double, with capacity utilization reaching 70-75% for billet and TMT.
items.quote: Roughly starting with the next quarter onwards, means it will be almost double, not the it may doubling the capacities will be mostly doubled.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton to remain around INR7,000, with potential improvement from higher volumes.
items.quote: INR7,000 margin. 40,000 to 50,000 tons will be the average. You can double the capacities, I have given the capacities will be doubled. So naturally your profitability and all will be increased.

items.statement: Reheating furnace and refurbishment capex to complete this year, operational by July end, contributing from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: And as far as the expansions which have been done already, they will come into operation by July end.

items.statement: IMR Group investing INR300 crores via share warrants, expected within six months.
items.quote: So, I think it will coming in next six months, we expect this to come in place.

items.statement: Steel demand outlook positive due to infrastructure, housing, and defense spending.
items.quote: Government-led infrastructure development, rising investments in construction and housing, increased spending on railways and defense infrastructure, and continued focus on domestic manufacturing are creating strong long-term demand drivers for the steel industry.

items.statement: Expanding into new markets and segments with new rebar products from reheating furnace.
items.quote: We have started one reheating furnace in our plant, which will enable us to manufacture up to 50,000 tons of new bars.

items.statement: War impact limited to diesel cost; raw materials sourced locally, insulating operations.
items.quote: Actually we are insulated as far as the war part is there. Only for some diesel cost it may have the on the transport, but otherwise we don't have much of impact because our basic raw materials what we procure are all locally only.

items.statement: Debt refinancing to reduce interest cost to around 9%, saving finance costs.
items.quote: Now, we would like to reduce further to the below sub-10% level rate, now around 9%. So, definitely there is going to be some savings on my cost thing, I mean finance cost going forward with this.

items.statement: Empaneled with major projects like Google's AI hub and ArcelorMittal, expecting supply opportunities.
items.quote: Yes, Yes, because basically we are also already empaneled with that the Google partner Adani who is building these things. And most of our supplies will be going from our Simhadri this thing.

items.statement: Planning 1 million ton green steel plant, groundbreaking expected soon.
items.quote: We have entered into an MOUs for making a 1 million ton green steel plant.

items.statement: Debt reduction target to negligible levels using internal accruals and warrant money.
items.quote: It may be from the internal accruals or from the share warrant -- share money. Once we get the money, we take a call on that because we have got some large investment plans also for the plant and -- which will started in phases.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 onwards production and EBITDA to improve significantly with reheating furnace operational.
items.quote: But now we are refurbishing and once the reheating furnace starts from the next quarter, we'll be having a great impact of the in the productions and EBITDA margins going forward in second quarter onwards.

items.statement: Pledged shares to be released after debt refinancing and improved finances.
items.quote: So we feel that when we do the refinancing, all our pledged shares will be released by the banks.

items.statement: Management expects EPS to cross INR 7 in FY27, up from INR 4.36 in FY26.
items.quote: Last year we were 4.36, and I am pretty decent if all things go well, we should be crossing 7 this year.

items.statement: Management expects to add 120-150 corporates per year over the next two years, with potential upside.
items.quote: I think the next two years, we are again just looking to add about 120 to 150 corporates a year, hopefully on a growing trajectory quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Management expects to add 150-200 companies this year, depending on market environment.
items.quote: So, we're looking at an addition of anywhere between 150 to 200 companies depending on the market environment and the quantum and the size of the company we are getting.

items.statement: Management expects to grow revenue at same pace as FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.
items.quote: We'll just look to grow it at probably the same pace as from FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.

items.statement: Management expects decent growth in SME loan book this year, with many proposals in pipeline.
items.quote: I think, there should be good growth in this year. I cannot commit on the numbers right now, but there should be decent growth this year. A lot of proposals in the pipeline.

items.statement: Management expects cost of funds to reduce in near term post rating upgrade, with offers from financial institutions.
items.quote: Not yet, but we are receiving a lot of offers from financial institutions to take funds from them. I think you should hear from us shortly.

items.statement: Gold loan syndication disbursed about INR 375 crores in Q4 FY26 through banking and NBFC partners.
items.quote: we disbursed about INR375 crores during the last quarter through our banking and NBFC partners, including ICICI, HDFC, RBL and Muthoot Finance.

items.statement: Corporate rejection rate is almost 60% due to CIBIL or banking issues, reflecting volatile market conditions.
items.quote: Our corporate rejection rate is almost as high as 60% now. We tend to reject corporates either on the basis of CIBIL or on the basis of banking.

items.statement: Cross-sell disbursements (INR 12 crores) exceeded EWA disbursements (INR 10 crores) in Q4 FY26.
items.value: INR10 crores EWA, INR12 crores cross-sell
items.quote: I would say INR10 crores and INR12 crores. INR10 crores is EWA and INR12 crores cross-sell.

items.statement: Cross-sell primarily includes personal, home, and gold loans; expanding into mutual funds and insurance.
items.quote: So cross-sell primarily right now we are doing personal loan, home loan, gold loan, but we are looking to expand into various other categories as well, including small-ticket mutual funds and insurance.

items.statement: Gross NPA for FY26 was INR 66 lakhs; INR 38 lakhs recovered and INR 23 lakhs written off.
items.quote: So, we had a gross NPA last year, which is including EWA plus our business loan and personal loan of INR66 lakhs. We recovered INR38 lakhs from our NPA pool and remaining as of March 31, we had written off INR23 lakhs.

items.statement: No new customers added to NPA in Q4 FY26; previous university issue fully recovered with overdue interest.
items.quote: Have we added any, have we added any new customer to an NPA? No, we have not added any new customer to the NPA.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded rating from BB+ to BBB-.
items.quote: I'm very pleased to share that CRISIL has upgraded our rating from BB+ to BBB-.

items.statement: Active EWA corporates about 185; total corporate clients 214 as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: Active are about 180, 185.

items.statement: Expects GST, tech, and renovation costs to drop to 3.7% of revenue by FY28, expanding EBITDA margins.
items.quote: We expect all these 3 expense heads to reduce to approximately 3.7% of revenue by FY28 and onwards, leading to corresponding expansion in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Plans to open about 2,000 rooms in FY27, similar to last year.
items.quote: Same click as last year, opened about 2,000 rooms.

items.statement: Expects to open 5,000 rooms annually in 2-3 years, based on current signings.
items.quote: we will be opening 5,000 rooms a year, because that is what we are signing now.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA flow-through of 75-80% and PAT margin of 60% for Lemon Tree.
items.quote: on a steady-state basis, hopefully, earlier rather than later, the growth of management fee income will translate to a flow-through of about 75%-80%, on a steady state basis.

items.statement: Government payment delays under new SPARSH portal and cash flow constraints impacted operations.
items.quote: the government has changed the payment system from the state and central government alliance. There is a new portal now in the capital of every state which ensures the share of the Central government and the state government.

items.statement: West Bengal election halted sewer work on Rs. 780 crore project, causing Rs. 70-80 crore quarterly revenue shortfall.
items.quote: from there only we were expecting minimum Rs. 70-80 crores revenue in the quarter with the reason that that has a Rs. 780 crores project.

items.statement: No current plan to raise funds; Board resolution for up to Rs. 300 crore is precautionary.
items.quote: But we assure you that now we don't have any plan to raise any funds right now.

items.statement: Pledge numbers reducing steadily and expected to be zero by end of next year.
items.quote: the pledge numbers have been reducing relatively steadily, and by the end of next year, it will be zero.

items.statement: Will continue focus on government water and sewerage sector; no diversification planned.
items.quote: we are doing 70% to 75% business from the water sector, which is likely to continue. We are bidding rigorously in the water sector.

items.statement: Management reiterates 25-30% CAGR growth guidance for FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: Talking about the current years and the future projections, we would like to stick to our growth projections of 25 to 30% CAGR, which will be we should be delivering this year as well.

items.statement: H2 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11% from 14% due to low-margin tile volume push; expected to improve this year.
items.quote: So, we introduced new design set of products, which we wanted to increase the volumes with. We were successful in increasing the volumes, but the sustainability for the margins was not supported enough.

items.statement: Gas supply disruption in Morbi led to 15-20 day price increase in March, passed on to customers.
items.quote: So the pricing was increased at the last few last month of March, approximately 15 to 20 days by which the impact has been passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Volumes increased 23-24% overall, in line with plan; no adverse impact from war so far.
items.quote: No, we have given the volumes that we had planned for. We have increased the volumes by about 23-24% roughly overall.

items.statement: Premium products like Marmi Bella and customized tiles expected to improve EBITDA and net margins this year.
items.quote: And our concentration should be well enough for improving the Guneet's previous question of improving the EBITDAs and the net margins for this year as well, including the customization of tiles that is the in-trend and requirement of the local end users.

items.statement: Debtors improved from 163 days to 114 days; trade receivables declined to ~63 crore.
items.quote: Though focused efforts on collections, inventory management and capital discipline, debtors improved substantially from 163 days to 114 days.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings reduced from 28.98 crores to 13.89 crores.
items.quote: Long-term borrowings reduced from 28.98 crores to 13.89 crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved by 44%.
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved meaningfully by 44%.

items.statement: B2B segment accounts for 80-82% of sales; B2C is balance.
items.quote: B2B has always been highest into comparatively roughly about 80-82%. Roughly about 80 to 82% in the B2B segment and the balance would be from the B2C segment.

items.statement: All warrants converted, including last promoter group warrant.
items.quote: The warrants have been converted, all of them. The last warrant that was remaining with the promoter group has been converted.

items.statement: Company plans further capex and expansions, announcements to be made soon.
items.quote: So yes we do have and things are on time and on place, stay tuned for more further announcements that we'll be making it in public.

items.statement: Plans to add 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, 8 asset-light, total keys past 3,000.
items.quote: During FY27 we plan to add 12 hotels totalling to 472 keys, out of which 8 would be asset-light side of the model taking the total key count past the 3,000 keys by FY27.

items.statement: Aims to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 by FY30.
items.quote: Over the next four years we plan to double the number of hotels from 42 hotels presently to 85 hotels and take the key count from 2,677 to 6,635.

items.statement: Targets surpassing 6,000 keys by FY30 with industry-leading occupancy.
items.quote: with a clear target of surpassing 6,000 keys by FY30, we remain focused on maintaining industry-leading occupancy levels and enhancing profitability across our portfolio.

items.statement: Five projects totaling 950 rooms at ~1.2 crore per room, ~1100 crores investment.
items.quote: we have approximately about five projects of Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass and Jaipur. These are totalling to 950 rooms with approx. 1.2 crore investment per room, which is about Rs. 1100 crores

items.statement: Total capital requirement ~1500 crores, funded mostly through internal accruals.
items.quote: So, there is a 1500 crores demand, which is being funded mostly through internal accruals, even if I take 250 crores as an EBITDA projection for five years.

items.statement: Expects additional cash flow improvement of ~70 crores from EM Bypass apartment sales this year.
items.quote: From EM Bypass sale, we expect additional cash flow improvement of close to 70 crores during the course of this year.

items.statement: Interest cost at 8.35% MCLR, expected to remain under control.
items.quote: The interest cost at present is 8.35%, which is the MCLR of the bank. So, it is expected to remain under that level only.

items.statement: Focus on ARR growth via room renovations in Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Vishakhapatnam.
items.quote: The focus is going to be on ARR. We are during the course of the year going to be carrying out room renovations across our properties. We are going to be renovating at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Vishakhapatnam.

items.statement: Demand-supply gap supports ARR improvement; supply lower by 200-300 bps.
items.quote: So demand side continues to be strong and the supply is lower by at least 200 to 300 basis points. So that should help us in improving ARRs, and that should drive our growth going forward in the existing properties.

items.statement: Geopolitical cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad due to Middle East war; situation stabilized.
items.quote: There have been cancellations because of the geopolitical situation and the war in the Middle East. Large significant cancellations did take place in Delhi as well as in Hyderabad. But things have stabilized now

items.quote: We have dropped the idea of making a central kitchen at New Delhi. We are going to be outsourcing the manufacturing of the products to a vendor and though that agreement has been signed

items.statement: Plans to double West Bengal room count to 800 over four years, including 218 keys at EM Bypass.
items.quote: we plan to add 218 keys on the ownership side of the model. items.value: high double-digit top line growth, EBITDA margins moving towards 5% range, PAT approaching FY '24 levels
items.quote: Our aim is to deliver growth in FY '27 with high double-digit top line growth. EBITDA margins moving towards 5% range and PAT approaching FY '24 levels as scale benefits, operating leverage and integration benefits begin to reflect in performance.

items.statement: Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 may still see supply constraints.
items.quote: In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.

items.statement: Passenger car service volumes to grow 10-12% in FY27, ASP up 12-13%.
items.value: 10% to 12% growth for FY '27 in terms of service volumes
items.quote: We're looking at least 10% to 12% growth for FY '27 in terms of service volumes in the Passenger Car segment.

items.statement: JLR volumes to rise to 550-600 units in FY27 from 380 last year.
items.quote: Assuming no such incident happen going forward and with our expansion in Nagpur, we are looking at the guidance of about 550 to 600 vehicles from Jaguar Land Rover this time

items.statement: No major acquisitions planned for FY27; focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
items.quote: But in terms of acquisitions, we are not looking at any high-value acquisitions this year. We're only looking at consolidation of our -- the acquisitions that we've done in the previous year and growing that business forward.

items.statement: Capex to be monitored; no additional debt beyond current business needs.
items.quote: Capex spends also will be more monitored. So, we would not be really looking at any additional debt on our books other than what is currently there for running our current business.

items.statement: Passenger car service EBITDA margin to reach 18-19%.
items.quote: But in terms of Passenger Car business, we should be reaching 18% to 19% EBITDA margins in terms of service margin.

items.statement: Demand indicators positive; entry-level recovery, lower discounting, new launches to support coming quarters.
items.quote: Demand indicators remain positive in spite of the war situation with inquiries and footfall showing healthy momentum. The recovery in entry-level vehicles, easing inventory levels, lower discounting and new model launches by OEM should support the business in the coming quarters.

items.statement: No noticeable demand impact from OEM price increases; supply constraints largely resolved.
items.quote: Post the price increase announcement by the OEMs, we have not seen much of a change actually. There is some bit of improvement in the booking, but that generally happens in every month end so cannot really relate whether it is because of that.

items.statement: Inventory levels to be kept below 30 days; debt mainly inventory-related.
items.quote: And going forward, we'll ensure that the inventory levels do not cross 30 days at any given point of time.

items.statement: FY27 core business revenue guidance of INR 4,500-5,000 crores, with scenario framework.
items.quote: So our FY 27 core business guidance was the EM of INR 4,500-5,000 crores.

items.statement: NCCCL targeting INR 850 crores revenue for FY27.
items.quote: we have guided around INR 850 crores target for NCCCL.

items.quote: the revenue -to-AUM ratio is expected to drop from 5.3% in FY 2026 to 2.85% in FY27 on a blended basis.

items.statement: NCCCL order book at INR 1,833 crores as of March 31, plus INR 870 crores added in first two months of FY27.
items.quote: The order book at the end of March stands at INR 1,833 crores. Having said that, within the first two months of this year, we have further added another INR 870 crores order from very known players

items.statement: NCCCL order book now stands at INR 2,600-2,700 crores after recent additions.
items.quote: when we speak today, the order book stands close to INR 2,600-2,700 crores.

items.statement: NCCCL EBITDA margin expected to remain at 9-10%, PAT margin 2-3%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin of 9-10% continues to be the industry the best norm in the industry is 9-10%, which is where we are, and that will continue more in the expanded order book. And the performance guidelines in terms of that will also remain as expected to be between that 2-3%.

items.statement: Neon Fund received SEBI approval, INR 1,800 crores with INR 500 crores green shoe, launch from Q2.
items.value: INR 1,800 crores + INR 500 crores green shoe
items.quote: It's a INR 1,800 crore fund with a INR 500 crore green shoe option.

items.statement: REIC Ops Fund winding up this year, performance fee likely in Q2.
items.quote: REIC Ops is we'll get round up this year with the last level winding up REIC Ops. And, therefore, the management fee will get booked feature.

items.quote: We also repaid 65% of acquisition debt, which stands at 38 crores as of March 31.

items.statement: UAE investments deferred over INR 500 crores due to West Asia conflict, timing not structural.
items.quote: we obviously saw some moderation in outcomes on account of Fairfield the conflict in the West Asia, which require us to defer certain investment decisions, which effectively was in excess of INR 500 crores only in the UAE

items.quote: 700 crores deal pipeline, almost 60-70% are at the term sheet stage, and the balance are under very serious evaluation.

items.statement: UAE pipeline of INR 2,000 crores, 50-60% at complete stage, renegotiating entries for better returns.
items.quote: for a pipeline of almost about INR 2,000 crores, we are now renegotiating the entries.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted to 55% fund management and 45% advisory, expected to continue shifting toward fund management.
items.quote: Both our advisory and asset management revenues are now approximately balanced at 45 % and 55% respectively, which is a meaningful structural shift from where we were two years back.

items.quote: when the white paper gets approved and the license is granted, which can take in some jurisdictions, it can take two to three quarters. So definitely, within this year, we are hopeful of going live with that product.

items.statement: Targets Q1 FY27 revenue to surpass Q4 FY26 revenue; expects healthy improvement.
items.quote: We will strive for improving our quarterly revenue base and will target Q1 FY27 revenue to surpass the Q4 FY26 revenues.

items.statement: Expects FY27 consolidated EBITDA margins to be better than FY26.
items.quote: From a profitable standpoint, we expect consolidated EBITDA margins to remain healthy and would be better than FY26.

items.statement: Expects FY27 to be a year of stronger growth and improved operating leverage.
items.quote: We therefore expect FY27 to be a year of stronger growth and improved operating leverage compared to the previous year.
